rt.jawab: If the 100 GWp program is finished in {n} years, the need is about {butuh} GWp per year (EST). Module makers serving the local market have {lokal} GWp of capacity per year, about {persen}% of that need. Of the {total} GWp per year in total, {ekspor} GWp is export oriented.
rt.k.ekspor_cat: includes {gw} GWp from makers serving both local and export
rt.k.program_cat: The first {n} projects of the {target} GWp target, not yet installed
rt.b.label: Programme need versus manufacturer capacity, GWp per year
rt.horizon_cat: Target {target} GWp divided by {n} years. The source gives no completion date, so this is a scenario.
rt.peta_label: Interactive map of solar module factories; pan, zoom, or click a circle
rt.peta_cat: Dots are city centres from the source table (METI approximation), not factory coordinates.
rt.cara1: Need per year = programme target {target} GWp divided by the number of years. The source gives no completion date, so 5, 8, or 10 years is a scenario (Hypothesis), not an official target.
rt.cara2: Manufacturer capacity is the MWp per year column of the DJEBTKE ESDM table on solar module manufacturers, summed as given. Export-oriented = export market plus makers serving both (18.3 GWp), so pure local supply is a lower bound.
rt.cara3: Manufacturers that have not reported capacity (cells marked -) are not counted. Installed factory capacity is not actual output.
rt.cara4: TKDN: local content level, percent per the source table. BMP: company benefit weight, as given in the source table. APAMSI: Indonesian Solar Module Manufacturers Association.
rt.cara5: The share of demand met by local supply is calculated (EST): capacity of manufacturers serving the local market divided by yearly demand.
rt.kutip: Cite as: METI Directory, PLTS supply chain page, data frozen {tanggal}. Manufacturer source: DJEBTKE ESDM table on solar module manufacturers in Indonesia.

as.tren_label: Trend in {metrik}, last 10 years, 10 ASEAN countries with Indonesia highlighted
as.cara1: Renewable electricity share: percent of electricity generation from renewable sources (Ember, via Our World in Data, CC BY 4.0). Renewable capacity: IRENASTAT, total renewables in MW (Brunei not listed). Electricity access: World Bank WDI, percent of population.
as.cara2: Ranks are computed by METI from each country's latest-year value; the latest year can differ between countries (shown on each bar). Trends use the last 10 yearly points.
as.cara3: Changes in the trend table are calculated (EST): percentage-point difference for share and access, relative change for capacity. Share measures the generation mix, capacity measures installed power. They are not the same.
as.kutip: Cite as: METI Directory, ASEAN page, data frozen {tanggal}. Sources: Ember via Our World in Data, IRENASTAT, World Bank WDI.

ins.pip.j: Tracked projects target {mw} MW of additions from {a} to {b}, peaking in {puncak} at {mwp} MW.
ins.pip.vs: equal to {persen}% of the {mw} MW installed renewable capacity
ins.pip.chart: Added capacity by target COD year (MW)
ins.pip.cara: Projects that are not yet operating and have a capacity and a target COD are grouped by their earliest COD year, then the first capacity of each project is summed per year. The comparison is the sum of installed renewable capacity across 38 provinces (HEESI). This is an EST figure, not an official schedule: phased projects are counted in full in their earliest year.
ins.pip.penting: The more MW pile up in one year, the more likely schedules slip.
ins.tel.j: {n} projects ({mw} MW) passed their target COD before {tahun} but are not recorded as operating.
ins.tel.cara: Projects whose status is not operating and whose earliest COD year is before {tahun} count as late. A project in several programs is counted in each. Source status can lag the field, so this is an EST figure, not a verdict of delay.
ins.tel.penting: Delays usually come from funding, land, or permits. The cause should be checked with the developer.
ins.cel.j: {prov} has the largest geothermal gap. {gap} MW of potential is not yet installed, and only {persen}% is used.
ins.cel.chart: Geothermal potential, installed and remaining by province (MW)
ins.cel.cara: Remaining potential = a province's geothermal potential minus its installed geothermal capacity. Only geothermal is computed because per province solar, wind and hydro potential is not yet available as readable data (RUEN annex). EST figure.
ins.cel.penting: Provinces with a large gap matter most for the national geothermal target.
ins.plt.j: Local module makers supply only {persen}% of the yearly need for the 100 GWp solar program, which is {lokal} of {butuh} GWp.
ins.plt.chart: Yearly need and local solar module supply (GWp)
ins.plt.cara: Need per year = the {target} GWp target divided by 10 years (a Hypothesis scenario, no official schedule yet). Local supply = capacity of makers serving the domestic market, summed from the DJEBTKE ESDM table. Supply uses installed factory capacity, not actual output.
ins.plt.penting: The gap has to be covered by imports or new factories. This affects module prices and local content.
ins.mix.j: {tek} makes up {a}% of the project pipeline but only {b}% of installed capacity.
ins.mix.chart: Pipeline and installed capacity by technology (% of capacity)
ins.mix.cara: Pipeline = capacity of projects not yet operating, per technology. Installed = installed capacity per technology, summed over 38 provinces (HEESI). Both are limited to technologies present in both datasets, then turned into percentages of their totals. The card highlights the technology with the largest difference. EST figure.
ins.mix.penting: A large gap means the generation mix will shift and the grid needs to be ready.
ins.reg.j: {n} regulations were issued in the last 12 months, against {m} in the 12 months before. Of {total} recorded regulations, {dicabut} are revoked.
ins.reg.ruu: Latest activity on the EBET bill: {judul} ({tanggal}).
ins.reg.cara: Regulations are counted by enactment date in two 365-day windows ending on the data freeze date. Revoked counts come from the status in the data. The RUU EBET item comes from the METI calendar. Data coverage limits the numbers, so this is EST.
ins.reg.penting: Frequent rule changes make schedules and prices hard to plan. Check the status before relying on a regulation.
ins.ber.j: {tek} got the most coverage in the last 30 days, with {n} stories against {m} in the 30 days before.
ins.ber.cara: News items with a technology expertise label are counted per technology in two 30-day windows ending on the data freeze date. One item can carry several technology labels. Unlabeled items are left out. EST figure.
ins.ber.penting: News volume follows public and market attention.
ins.fin.j: State green sukuk allocated USD {usd} million to renewable energy (2018 to 2024, {persen}% of the total). The initial JETP commitment is USD {jetp} billion.
ins.fin.chart: Cumulative green sukuk allocation 2018 to 2024 (USD million)
ins.fin.cara: Figures are taken as published from the 2025 Green Sukuk Allocation and Impact Report (DJPPR Ministry of Finance): cumulative allocation to the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency sectors and to projects owned by the Ministry of Energy. ins.cara1: All cards are calculated in the browser from Direktori METI data files when the page opens. The finding text is not hand-written. Only the explanatory sentence and the note on each card are.
ins.cara2: The EST label marks figures METI calculated from source data. The Hypothesis label marks figures that rest on an assumption, for example a 10-year schedule for the 100 GWp solar program.
ins.cara3: The Most important order is a METI team judgment of each finding's impact, not an automatic score. Cards whose data is not available, such as IDXCarbon carbon trading and green sukuk, stay hidden until the data arrives.
ins.cara4: Each card carries its source, data date and a denominator of the form n of N rows, so the share of data used is visible.
ins.kutip: Cite as: METI Directory, Insight page, data frozen {tanggal}. The source of each figure is on its card.

met.alur.j: From public source to on-screen figure, six steps
met.alur.sub: Every step can be checked; no figure is typed by hand.
met.alur.alt: Six steps: harvest, link, compute, label, curate, publish
met.alur.panen: Scripts fetch data from official sites, open files, and news. Each file is stored with its source address and fetch date.
met.alur.sambung: Organization, project, and region names are matched and standardized, aliases merged, so one entity does not appear twice.
met.alur.hitung: Derived figures such as shares, totals, and differences are computed from source data with open formulas. Cells without data stay empty, not guessed.
met.alur.label: Each figure carries its origin: official, study, media, or party statement. Computed results are labeled EST and those using assumptions are labeled Hypothesis.
met.alur.kurasi: The METI team reviews rows flagged for review. Users can report corrections, and every change is logged.
met.alur.terbit: Data that passes checks is frozen and published. Automatic test gates reject data without a source or date.
met.alur.prinsip: Principle: only publicly traceable data, formulas that can be checked, and an origin label on every figure.
met.tb.j: Labels showing where a figure comes from
met.tb.sub: A figure always carries its label. Labels are not a quality ranking, but origin and method.
met.tb.resmi: From documents or data of a government agency or official body.
met.tb.kajian: From research reports or think tanks with an open method.
met.tb.kajian.contoh: Solar potential from the potential atlas.
met.tb.media: Reported by media; not yet confirmed by an official document.
met.tb.media.contoh: Investment value from a project news item.
met.tb.kata: A statement by a company or related party, not verified by a third party.
met.tb.kata.contoh: Capacity target from a developer website.
met.tb.est: Estimate: a METI computation from source data, not a figure announced by the source.
met.tb.est.contoh: A developer's share of total capacity.
met.tb.hip: Uses assumptions; only valid if the assumptions hold, and the calculation is open.
met.tb.hip.contoh: A 10-year schedule for the 100 GWp solar target.
met.tb.tinjau: Extracted automatically and not yet read by a person, or failed a cross-check.
met.tb.tinjau.contoh: Rows from OCR of a scanned document.
met.sc.sub: Compiled from the source metadata of each data file. An empty license means it is not yet recorded in the file.
met.sc.cat: List built {tgl}. The update date is when the dataset file was built, not the source's schedule.
met.rp.porsi: Developer and funder names are normalized and aliases merged before computing. Shares are computed against the capacity of named owners, not all projects. Report data only holds the top 15 rows.
met.rp.porsi.rumus:
share (%) = MW of one developer ÷ MW of all named owners × 100
MW of one developer = sum of MW across all aliases of the same name
met.rp.banding: Only comparable metrics are compared. Periods before news recording began and the current year are flagged, not shown as zero.
met.rp.banding.rumus:
change = value this period − value last period
comparable when both periods are fully recorded
met.rp.nilai: Values come from project data, split into reported and estimated. Financing programs and loans are separated from power projects and not counted as RE projects.
met.rp.nilai.rumus:
coverage = power projects with a value ÷ all power projects
programs or loans are in neither numerator nor denominator

met.bt.koreksi.isi: Open the profile of the organization or project with wrong data, then use the Report a correction button. Corrections are reviewed by the METI team and changes are logged.

kl.a.head: Head (m)
kl.a.sumber: CAPEX and OPEX ranges follow IRENA, Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2023, and the ESDM/DEA Technology Catalogue 2023. The 8 percent WACC, the rate, and the generic power curve are METI assumptions.
kl.dekat.sub: The five tracker projects with the closest point to this location.
kl.cara1: Solar: output = PSH (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN irradiance, kWh per m2 per day) x 365 x PR 0.8 x MW.
kl.cara2: Wind: WS50M speed scaled to hub height (power law 0.14), Weibull k = 2 distribution, generic power curve (cut-in 3, rated 12, cut-out 25 m/s), less losses.
kl.cara3: LCOE = (CAPEX x CRF + OPEX) divided by energy per kW per year, with CRF from WACC and lifetime. No degradation, tax, construction interest, or grid cost.
kl.cara4: The benchmark uses the base coefficient of Presidential Reg. 112/2022 by capacity; the location factor F is taken as 1. Micro-hydro uses the small hydro tier.
kl.cara5: The result is a Hypothesis and needs a field study, wind or flow measurement, and permits before it informs a decision.

brt.an.sumber: Headlines from berita.json and the media_tier.json domain table; article text is not stored. Counts use keywords in headlines (EST). Data as of
brt.an.ramai.sub: Similar headlines grouped within a 72 hour window, last 30 days.
brt.an.ramai.cara: How it is computed: headlines are split into words, common words dropped; two headlines are one story when word overlap over union (Jaccard) is at least 0.4 and they were published within 72 hours. Automatic grouping, can be wrong (EST).
brt.an.ramai.kosong: No story has been covered by two or more outlets in the last 30 days.
brt.an.isu.sub: EBET issue dictionary on headlines: 24 hours, 7 days, and change versus the previous week.
brt.an.isu.cara: How it is computed: a headline counts when it contains an issue keyword. Windows end at the newest story in the data. Percent = this week versus last week; blank when last week is zero. Clicking filters the list by the issue's main keyword, so the list count can be lower (EST).
brt.an.isu.kosong: No issue recorded in the last two weeks.
brt.an.tren.sub: Trend line per topic and per outlet; click a card to see the evidence headlines.
brt.an.tren.cara: How it is computed: headlines per day over 30 days up to the newest story. Topics from automatic technology labels (EST). Each card uses its own scale, so line heights are not comparable across cards.
brt.an.tier.sub: Stories by media tier; pick a tier to see the latest headlines.
brt.an.tier.cara: How it is computed: each domain maps to one tier via the METI editorial table (data/media_tier.json); unlisted domains fall to national (Indonesian) or international. The classification is not an official ranking (Hypothesis).
brt.an.desak.j: {hl} headlines carry a demand or request
brt.an.desak.sub: Headlines with words like urge or call for, grouped by what they ask.
brt.an.desak.cara: How it is computed: a headline counts when it has a word like urge, request, push, demand or propose plus a category keyword. One headline can fall in several categories. Word matching, not reading the article (EST).
brt.an.desak.kosong: No demand headlines in this data.
brt.an.keb.sub: Last 30 days of headlines on rules, auctions, tariffs, deadlines or launches.
brt.an.keb.cara: How it is computed: word rules on headlines, last 30 days. Links to regulations or the calendar per category; no guarantee a headline matches an entry there (EST).
brt.an.keb.kosong: No policy news in the last 30 days.
brt.an.dunia.j: {hl} English stories from foreign outlets this week
brt.an.dunia.j30: {hl} articles on Indonesian energy in foreign media in 30 days, most from {n}

brt.an.dunia.cara: How it is computed: English stories, country from the outlet domain (Indonesian English-language outlets excluded). Generic .com, .org, .net domains with no hint count as United States, an estimate (EST).

ix.title: Open index: provincial readiness and project health | Direktori METI
ix.deskripsi: Readiness index for 38 provinces and health of renewable energy projects, labelled hypothesis, with formulas, weights, and checkable sources.
ix.lead: Two 0 to 100 scores with checkable formulas: readiness of 38 provinces and the health of each project.
ix.peta.sub: Darker means more ready. Click a province for component details.
ix.peta_gagal: The province map did not load.

ix.p.kosong: No data (left out of the calculation)
ix.m.j: How it is computed, weights, sources, and limits
ix.m.ringkas: Scores run 0 to 100 from normalised, weighted components. A component without data is left out and the remaining weights are rescaled; it is never silently filled with zero.
ix.m.rumus.prov: Score = sum(weight x component score) / sum(weights of present components). Percentile = (count of smaller values + half the other ties) / (n - 1) x 100. Min-max = (x - min) / (max - min) x 100.
ix.m.min: Only provinces with at least {p}% of the weight present are ranked.
ix.m.rumus.proyek: Two separate dimensions. Health = sum(weight x signal) / sum(weights of present signals), from real signals only: schedule (100 minus 40 per year past planned COD without operating, floor 0; 0 if cancelled) and status (0 if delayed, stopped, stalled, or cancelled). The "problem" label applies to health only. Data completeness = age of latest news (100 if 180 days or less, 0 at 730 days or more or no news; active projects only) and fields (owner, capacity, location, source). A completeness score below 75 gets the neutral label "Data needs updating", not a problem.

lal.dim.24j: The tables below use today and yesterday for the 24 hour period.
lal.cara.sub: Everything is counted on the server, without storing IP addresses.
lal.cara.1: Every requested page is counted in the Worker before the sign-in gate, so crawlers that only reach the sign-in page are still recorded per path.
lal.cara.2: A unique visitor per day is a salted hash of IP and browser. The salt changes daily and the old salt is deleted, so yesterday's hash can no longer be matched.
lal.cara.3: AI answers are assistants opening a page for someone (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User). AI search and training are crawlers such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot, Amazonbot, and Exa. Search engines are Googlebot, Bingbot, Applebot, and DuckDuckBot.
lal.cara.4: Crawlers that publish their official IP ranges are checked daily. A match is verified; outside the list is treated as fake and not counted.
lal.cara.5: Not counted as people: hosting or cloud networks, scripts and scanners, and requests without browser signals.
lal.cara.6: A click from an AI answer is a visit by a person arriving from an AI assistant referrer such as chatgpt.com, claude.ai, or perplexity.ai.

mak.a1: A row with the same name, technology, and capacity as another project is treated as a duplicate; only one enters the total.
mak.a2.j: A subsidiary inside its parent is not counted twice
mak.a2: Capacity owned by {anak} ({mw} MW on one project) is already inside the {induk} group. The subsidiary owner row is shown but not added to the group total.
mak.a3.j: A joint venture is counted once
mak.a3: A joint venture's capacity enters the total once, in full. Each owner's share is noted in the owner column when the source gives a percentage.
mak.a4: The large projects page only lists capacity of {mw} MW or more. MW and MWp are mixed, so totals are labelled EST; other units such as tonnes per day are not summed.
mak.a5: Batteries are not generators, so their MW are not added to generation. Cancelled or postponed projects leave the total and move to the halted projects page.
mak.keluar.s: Each row below is in the data but does not add to the MW total, with the reason.
mak.al.tidak_diungkap.ket: The source deliberately does not say, for example RUPTL only writes IPP with no company name.
mak.al.belum_bersumber.ket: No public source found yet; it can be filled when one appears.
mak.al.di_luar_cakupan.ket: The row is not a megawatt-scale plant, for example a development loan or programme, so the column is not relevant.
mak.al.tidak_berlaku.ket: The column has no meaning for that row, for example a COD target for an operating project.
mak.kerja.s: Construction and manufacturing in person-years per MW, O&M in people per MW, multiplied by {pengali} for non-OECD Asia. Manufacturing is not counted because most of it happens outside Indonesia. Hydro above {ambang} MW uses the large factor (METI assumption).

bl.title: Electricity costs and prices | METI Directory
bl.deskripsi: Electricity cost by technology: LCOE for Indonesia and the world, solar module prices over time, and PLN generation cost (BPP) by system, with source, year, and evidence level.
bl.lead: What electricity costs from each technology, how it has fallen, and where Indonesia stands. Every figure is sourced, dated, and labelled with its evidence level.
bl.t.lcoe: World solar electricity cost fell {hl} between {a} and {b}
bl.t.banding: In {tahun}, Indonesia's onshore wind LCOE was {hl} US cents/kWh, {x} times the world average ({w})
bl.t.ebtfosil: {hl} renewable technologies cost less than the {tahun} national BPP ({bpp} US cents/kWh)
bl.t.modul: Solar module prices fell from {a} USD/W ({ta}) to {hl} ({tb})
bl.t.bpp: PLN national BPP moved from {a} ({ta}) to {hl} ({tb}), a change of {p}%
bl.t.celah: There are {hl} data limitations readers should know about
bl.s.lcoe: World average LCOE by technology, 2010 to latest, constant 2025 USD
bl.s.banding: Latest available LCOE by country, constant 2025 USD
bl.s.ebtfosil: Latest world renewable LCOE against national BPP (dashed line)
bl.s.modul: World solar module price, USD per watt, 1975 to latest
bl.s.bpp: PLN generation cost of supply under ESDM decrees
bl.s.celah: What cannot yet be shown, and why
bl.n.lcoe: LCOE is the average cost per kWh over the life of a new plant. World values are IRENA weighted averages. Percentage changes are derived (EST).
bl.n.banding: The latest year differs by country; compare with the year in view. IRENA lists Indonesian LCOE only for onshore wind, 2017 to 2020. The ratio to the world is derived (EST).
bl.n.ebtfosil: Two different price bases: LCOE is in 2025 USD, BPP is in rupiah at the exchange rate of its year. BPP is the blended cost of all PLN generation, not a fossil LCOE. The comparison is indicative (EST).
bl.n.modul: Since 2010 this is the European market benchmark (pvXchange), not Indonesian import prices.
bl.n.bpp: One decree per BPP year; only four years are available. The percentage change between first and last year is derived (EST) and not inflation-adjusted.
bl.top: 12 systems with the highest BPP in {tahun}, Rp/kWh
bl.skala.label: Axis scale
bl.celah.1: IRENA lists Indonesian LCOE only for onshore wind, 2017 to 2020; Indonesian solar, geothermal, and hydro are absent from the releases read. Indonesian LCOE from IESR and Agora is in PDF form: needs an owner download.
bl.celah.2: Battery and inverter prices over time are not openly available (BNEF series cannot be redistributed; Our World in Data refuses its CSV). Needs an owner download: IRENA Electricity Storage Costs or IEA reports.
bl.celah.3: Module prices since 2010 are the European benchmark (pvXchange), not Indonesian import prices; BPS import data needs an owner download.
bl.celah.4: Fossil LCOE is not included (the IRENA releases read cover renewables only); national BPP serves as a blended benchmark, not a fossil LCOE. Fossil subsidies (IESR) need an owner download.
bl.celah.5: BPP is available only for 2016, 2017, 2018, and 2020 (the decree files received); 2015, 2019, and 2021 onward are missing.
bl.celah.6: Indicative market prices by technology have no dated public source read; Presidential Regulation 112/2022 tariffs are already in the finance data.

tr.title: Power transition: targets, systems, carbon | METI Directory
tr.deskripsi: Distance to renewable targets, RUKN and KEN scenarios, power system health per PLN system, and carbon market and credits, with a source and date on every figure.
tr.lead: How far the renewable targets are, how ready the power systems are, and how active the carbon market is, from official documents and data already collected.
tp.deskripsi: One research report for each energy topic: the Indonesian picture, policy, technology, international benchmarks, money, and lessons from projects, with a source and date on every figure.
tr.g.target_sub: How many MW per year are needed, what official documents say for 2030 and 2060, and how far the 100 GW program has come.
tr.g.sistem_sub: Peak load, reserve margin, energy mix, and plant performance per PLN system.
tr.g.karbon_sub: Carbon exchange, grid emission factors, regulation, and renewable project credits.
tr.src.program: 100 GW solar program (METI analysis of news and documents)
tr.celah.sub: Renewable capacity that must be added each year to reach the RUPTL, RUKN, and KEN targets, against the 2015-2024 pace. Derived figures, not forecasts.
tr.celah.judul: The 2025-2034 RUPTL target needs {hl} MW of new renewables per year, {kali} times the 2015-2024 pace
tr.celah.laju: Dashed line: the 2015-2024 pace of {mw} MW per year.
tr.celah.grafik: Renewable capacity needed per year by target
tr.celah.catatan: Mix targets are converted to MW by proxy: renewable share times the KEN midpoint electricity demand, divided by an added-capacity factor of 0.35 (range 0.25 to 0.45). The RUPTL and RUKN 2060 targets come directly from stated capacity.
tr.tambah.sub: Year-on-year change in installed renewable capacity from the Electricity Statistics, with the monthly average.
tr.tambah.judul: Renewables grew by an average of {hl} MW per year ({bln} MW per month) over {a}-{z}
tr.tambah.grafik: Renewable capacity added per year in MW
tr.tambah.catatan: The Statistics publish no monthly series, so the monthly figure is the annual figure divided by 12. 2020 compares two different Statistics editions, so its value is understated.
tr.skenario.sub: Official KEN, RUKN, and RUPTL targets next to actual figures and IESR study comparators.
tr.sk.judul: RUKN targets {hl}% renewables in electricity production by 2060, up from {y30}% in 2030
tr.sk.grafik: Renewable share of electricity production: actual and RUKN target
tr.sk.catatan: Actual figures use the Ember generation definition (via Our World in Data); RUKN uses its own definition, so the two are not strictly comparable. KEN targets use primary energy, not electricity.
tr.rukn.sub: Annual renewable share targets in electricity production under RUKN, compared with actual figures where available.
tr.rukn.judul: The RUKN target rises from {hl}% in 2025 to {z}% in 2060, with renewables passing fossil from {tahun_ebt}
tr.rukn.kaki: No 2025 actual figure is available from a readable source. A negative gap means actual is below target; the RUKN and Ember definitions differ.
tr.dekomp.sub: The change in renewable share is split into the effect of added renewable output and the effect of total demand growth.
tr.dk.judul_naik: The renewable generation share rose {hl} percentage points from {a} to {z}: added renewables gave {e} points, demand growth held back {p} points
tr.dk.judul_turun: The renewable generation share fell {hl} percentage points from {a} to {z}: added renewables gave {e} points, demand growth held back {p} points
tr.dk.grafik: Annual change in renewable share in percentage points, split into two effects
tr.dk.catatan: Change in share = (renewables this year - renewables last year) / total output this year + renewables last year x (1 / total this year - 1 / total last year). The two terms add up exactly to the change in share.
tr.pl.judul: The {hl} GW solar program through {th}: {n} tracked projects with {mw} MW
tr.pl.grafik: Solar capacity: installed, tracked, first phase, cooperative track, and target
tr.pl.catatan: The 17 GW, 80 GW, and 100 GW figures come from news; the draft presidential regulation had not been issued at the last check and the target is not yet in RUKN or RUPTL. Tracked projects are METI projects that match the program, not necessarily official parts of it.
tr.peta.sub: Colour follows the chosen metric, in five classes by rank across 16 systems.
tr.peta.judul_rm: The 2025 reserve margin is lowest at {hl} in {min} and highest at {v2} in {maks}
tr.peta.judul_tumbuh: Peak load grows slowest at {hl} per year in {min} and fastest at {v2} in {maks}
tr.peta.judul_ebt: The 2034 renewable mix is lowest at {hl} in {min} and highest at {v2} in {maks}
tr.peta.label: Province map coloured by PLN system
tr.peta.tanpa: No power balance table (Riau Islands are served by the Batam system)
tr.peta.gagal: The map could not be loaded.
tr.peta.catatan: Province-to-system mapping is approximate: each province is given its main system, though some provinces are served by several small systems. Riau Islands have no table in this RUPTL.
tr.p.sumber: RUPTL 2025-2034, {tabel}, RE Base scenario. Emission intensity is derived (EST).
tr.sistem.sub: Peak load, reserve margin, and energy mix for each system from the RUPTL 2025-2034 power balance, RE Base scenario.
tr.sistem.judul: Net peak load across 16 PLN systems grows {hl} per year, from {a} MW in 2025 to {z} MW in 2034
tr.sistem.catatan: Reserve margin is system dependable capacity minus net peak load, divided by net peak load. PLN's reasonable range is discussed in RUPTL chapter II; above 40 percent means a thick reserve.
tr.beban.sub: National peak load 2015-2024 and sales per PLN region in 2024.
tr.beban.judul: National peak load rose from {a} MW in 2015 to {z} MW in 2024, {hl} per year
tr.beban.grafik: National peak load per year in MW
tr.beban.unit: Unit: GW (MW detail in the tooltip).
tr.beban.catatan: Highest monthly peak across all systems, grid and isolated, including Batam Bintan; 2024 runs only through October. Statistics 2024 does not publish peak load per province.
tr.kapasitas.sub: National capacity factor by plant type, and geothermal and hydro by province.
tr.kap.judul: Coal plants nationwide ran at a {hl} capacity factor in {y}, leaving about {idle}% of theoretical capacity unused
tr.kap.grafik: National capacity factor by plant type, percent
tr.kap.catatan: Capacity factor = generation divided by installed capacity x 8,760 hours, from Ember data. Capacity includes captive plants, so it is not PLN alone. Bioenergy and geothermal are not shown because Ember's capacity does not match its generation.
tr.kap.catatan_prov: Estimated provincial capacity factor: PLN output (including purchases from IPPs) divided by capacity of all operators. Values outside 0 to 100 percent are shown as a dash because the two Statistics tables do not match. Per-operator geothermal and hydro performance needs the operators' annual reports.
tr.vre.sub: Named solar and wind plans against storage plans per RUPTL region.
tr.vre.judul: Planned storage of {hl} exceeds the {vre} MW of named solar and wind in the RUPTL
tr.vre.grafik: Named solar and wind against storage per region, MW
tr.vre.unit: Unit: MW. Eastern region = Sulawesi, Maluku, Papua, and Nusa Tenggara.
tr.vre.catatan: Only named projects in the RUPTL annex; dispersed solar and wind quotas are not counted, so actual solar and wind are larger. Per-system variable penetration limits are not published in a readable table.
tr.vre.iesr: IESR: solar and wind supplied under {v} percent of electricity generation in {y}.
tr.bursa.sub: Volume, value, and average price of monthly carbon exchange trading.

tr.pajak.catatan: Presidential Regulation 110/2025 is in force and replaces 98/2021. The carbon tax rate and rollout are not in the local regulation corpus: the text of Law 7/2021 and related ministerial regulations needs an owner download, so this page states no rate.
tr.kredit.sub: Indonesian renewable projects on Gold Standard and Verra: credits issued and retired.
tr.kr.judul: {n} renewable projects on Gold Standard and Verra issued {hl} million tCO2e of credits, {pen} million already retired
tr.kr.grafik: Credits issued and retired per technology, million tCO2e
tr.kr.catatan: Gold Standard is read from its public platform; Verra is read from the Berkeley VROD copy (CC BY 4.0), not the Verra registry, so its evidence level is third-party. Credit prices and buyers are unavailable. Non-energy projects are excluded.
tr.celahdata.sub: Items that cannot be shown yet because the source is out of reach; they need an owner download.
tr.celah.kurtailmen: Curtailment (variable renewable energy discarded): no public figure per system in RUPTL 2025-2034 or Electricity Statistics 2024. Needs PLN system operation reports or ESDM data.
tr.celah.operator: Capacity factor per geothermal and hydro operator: operators' annual reports have not been collected. The page uses estimated provincial figures.
tr.celah.faktor_emisi: Official ESDM grid emission factor per system: the document is not in the local corpus. The page uses intensity derived from the RUPTL tables.
tr.celah.pajak: Carbon tax rate and its postponement: the text of Law 7/2021 and its implementing rules is not in the regulation corpus.
tr.celah.srn: SRN PPI status per renewable project: the SRN portal is not collected. What appears are projects listed on IDXCarbon and the Gold Standard and Verra registries.
tr.celah.bulanan: Monthly renewable capacity additions: ESDM and PLN press releases carry no structured monthly series; the page uses the annual average divided by 12.
tr.celah.serap: Variable renewable penetration limit per system and the Ember absorption curve: no readable table in the RUPTL; the page uses named project plans.
tr.cara.sub: Derived formulas and limits of interpretation.
tr.cara.celah: MW per year: for capacity targets, required additions divided by years; for mix targets, renewable share times the KEN midpoint electricity demand, divided by the added-capacity factor and 8,760 hours. Results are EST and depend on assumptions.
tr.cara.tambah: Annual additions: year-on-year difference in installed renewable capacity; per month = annual addition divided by 12.
tr.cara.dekomp: Decomposition: share = renewables divided by total output; the change in share is split into the added-renewables effect and the growing-total effect, and the two sum exactly to the change.
tr.cara.fk: Capacity factor = generation divided by (capacity x 8,760 hours). National from Ember; provincial from Electricity Statistics 2024.
tr.cara.emisi: Emission intensity = a system's annual GHG emissions (million tonnes CO2) times 1,000 divided by annual production (GWh), in tCO2 per MWh.
tr.cara.peta: Reserve margin = (system dependable capacity - net peak load) divided by net peak load, as written in the RUPTL power balance tables; map colour classes follow the rank across 16 systems.
tr.cara.kutip: How to cite: METI Network Platform, Power transition page, data as of {tanggal}, with the original source of each figure.

met.pw.j: How the province map and province profile are calculated
met.pw.sub: The formula for each metric and card; sources and data years are stated, empty cells are never filled with guesses
met.pw.terpasang: RE plant capacity per province from HEESI 2025 (Ministry of Energy), Table 6.4.9: hydro (large and mini/micro combined), geothermal, solar, wind and bioenergy, summed. Official figures, not recalculated. Zero means recorded zero; a dash means the source has no figure.
met.pw.potensi: Sum of potential by technology. Solar (Table 44), wind (46), mini and micro hydro (40), bioenergy (42), practical marine (48) and hydro (37) from RUEN, Presidential Reg. 22/2017, Annex I, 2015 data; geothermal (resources + reserves) from HEESI 2025 Table 6.5.1. A province absent from a table is shown as no data (hatched), not zero.
met.pw.hidro.j: Why hydro is filled for only some provinces
met.pw.hidro: RUEN Table 37 is organised by region group: 14 rows, eight of them a single province (Papua, Aceh, West Kalimantan, North Sumatra, West Java, Central Java, East Java, Maluku) and six multi-province groups. The 14 rows match the document total, 75,091 MW. Group figures are not split evenly among member provinces; they appear as a group note in the map tooltip and province profile.
met.pw.papua: RUEN uses 34 provinces (2015 data, before the Papua split). The Papua and West Papua parent figures are shown on the two parent provinces, labelled 2015 data, before the split. The four new provinces (South, Central, Highland Papua, Southwest Papua) have no data; no even split is made because there is no basis for allocation.
met.pw.sisa: Per technology: potential minus installed capacity, floored at zero, then summed over technologies that have both figures. RUEN potential is 2015 and HEESI installed capacity is 2025, so this is an indication, not an official headroom. For parent Papua, installed capacity covers only today's Papua province.
met.pw.proyek: The number of projects in the METI directory located in that province. Projects without a province are not on the map; their count is stated under the map.
met.pw.rued: A province counts as having RUED when its regional regulation is recorded at peraturan.bpk.go.id. The percentage target is shown only when readable from the text; automatic quotes are marked not yet reviewed.
met.pw.capaian: Ratio = realisation divided by target. Realisation: RE share of total installed capacity in 2024 (Electricity Statistics). Target: 2025 RE primary energy mix in the RUED regulation. The measures differ, so it is labelled Hypothesis. Achieved at 100% or more, on track at 75% or more, behind below that.
met.pw.peringkat: Ranking uses the selected metric among provinces that have data. The median and range on the Comparison card are computed from the same provinces with data.
met.pw.emisi: Satellite and Climate TRACE model estimates per plant (tCO2e per year), not operator reports. The province total is the sum of the plants on record.

st.title: Strategic review of Indonesia renewables | METI Directory
st.deskripsi: Analysis derived from open data: target gaps, province and technology opportunity map, project risk radar, market concentration, funding flows, and market signals. Formulas and sources are open.
st.lead: Analysis derived from the data collected so far: how far the targets are, where the opportunities lie, which projects are at risk, who holds the market, where money flows, and where coverage is heading. Not AI, not a calculator: fixed formulas, open sources.
st.u1: times the historical pace for the RUPTL 2034 capacity target
st.u2: year the {target} mix target ({tahun}) is reached if the trend continues
st.u3: high-risk projects of {total} in the pipeline
st.g.kesenjangan_sub: Mix and capacity targets (KEN, RUKN, RUPTL, NZE) compared with the annual realisation path.
st.g.peta_sub: Combined score for 38 provinces and 8 technologies from seven numeric components.
st.g.radar_sub: Planned and under-construction projects with measurable warning signs and a checklist.
st.g.konsentrasi_sub: Who holds operating capacity, how shares shift, and who grows fastest.

st.ring.judul: {hl} key findings from the data collected so far
st.ring.sub: Generated automatically from the analyses below
st.ring.catatan: Generated automatically from platform data as of {tgl}; each sentence uses the same numbers as the section it links to. Use the button below to print the whole review as PDF.
st.f.kapasitas: The RUPTL 2025-2034 renewable capacity addition target requires {perlu} MW per year, {kali} times the historical pace of {laju} MW per year.
st.f.bauran: The renewable generation mix of {real} in 2024 must reach {target} by {tahun}; at a trend of {tren} points per year the target is reached around {capai}.
st.f.tek_kejar: {tek} is furthest from pace: the named RUPTL pipeline needs {perlu} MW per year, {kali} times the historical {laju} MW.
st.f.sel_unggul: Highest opportunity cell: {tek} in {prov} with a combined score of {skor}.
st.f.prov_unggul: Province with the highest average score across eight technologies: {prov} ({skor}).
st.f.radar: {tinggi} of {total} pipeline projects are high risk, representing {mw} MW.
st.f.cod: {n} pipeline projects are past their COD target, {mw} MW of {total} MW in the pipeline.
st.f.hhi: Ownership of {tek} is the most concentrated: HHI {hhi}, with {terbesar} holding {pangsa}.
st.f.bumn: The state-owned share of renewable capacity with a named owner fell from {dari} ({a}) to {ke} ({z}).
st.f.celah_dana: Public funding for {tek} is only {pangsa_dana} of the total although it holds {pangsa_mw} of pipeline MW: reallocation gap {celah} (all technologies {total}).
st.f.momentum: The share of news on {tek} rose {selisih} points to {akhir} in the last full months.
st.bauran.sub: Renewable generation mix, targets and trend path
st.bauran.judul: The renewable mix must rise {hl} points per year for the RUPTL {tahun} target, the historical trend is only {tren} points
st.bauran.grafik: Renewable generation mix 2015 to 2034: realisation, trend, RUKN path and RUPTL target
st.bauran.catatan: Realisation from Our World in Data (percent of electricity generation); generation targets from RUKN and RUPTL. KEN rows use the Energy Institute substitution method for primary energy, a different measure from generation. Trend = linear regression 2015-2024.
st.bauran.kes: The {target} target for {tahun} is reached only around {capai} if the 2015-2024 trend continues, {telat} years late. Meeting it on time needs a structural change in the pace of renewable additions, not an extension of the trend.
st.kap.sub: Capacity added per year needed against the historical pace
st.kap.judul: The RUPTL capacity target requires {hl} MW added per year, {kali} times the historical pace of {laju} MW per year
st.kap.grafik: Bars of renewable capacity added per year needed for each target, dashed line the historical pace
st.kap.catatan: Historical pace = (renewable capacity 2024 minus 2015) divided by 9 years (Electricity Statistics). Need = MW gap divided by remaining years. Year reached = start year plus gap divided by historical pace.
st.kap.kes: {dok}: at the historical pace the capacity addition target is reached around {capai}, and the needed pace is {kali} times the current one.
st.tek.sub: IRENA historical pace against the named RUPTL pipeline need
st.tek.judul: {hl} is furthest from its historical pace: it needs {kali} times
st.tek.grafik: Dots of historical pace and annual need for each technology
st.tek.catatan: Of the {total} MW RUPTL addition target, {nama} MW is named by technology (planned and under construction); the other {sisa} MW is dispersed or quota without detail, so the per-technology need is a lower bound. Historical pace: IRENA capacity 2015 to 2025.
st.tek.kes: {tek} fills its named pipeline only around {tahun} at the historical pace, while its target year is {target}.
st.peta.sub: Score 0 to 100 per province and technology, click a cell for the numeric reasons
st.peta.judul: {hl} of {total} province and technology cells have a combined score; the highest is {tek} in {prov}
st.peta.label: Province and technology opportunity score matrix
st.peta.sel_kosong: {prov}, {tek}: not enough data for a score
st.peta.pilih: Select a cell in the matrix to see score components, numeric reasons and the conclusion.
st.peta.kurang_n: Only {n} components have data for this cell; a score needs at least three, so it is not computed.
st.peta.petunjuk: Combined score = weighted average of the components that exist (weights in the method section); components without data are left out of the denominator, not filled with zero. Marine and nuclear are not in the matrix for lack of installed capacity or pipeline.
st.k.sisa: Potential {pot} MW minus installed {ter} MW = remaining {sisa} MW; score = percentile among provinces.
st.k.tarif: Local BPP {bpp} US cents per kWh against the Perpres 112 benchmark tariff of {tarif} cents (tier {tingkat}, location factor {F}); BPP to tariff ratio {r}, the higher the easier for PLN to buy.
st.k.ruptl: RUPTL planned and under-construction pipeline in this cell is {mw} MW; score = percentile among provinces.
st.k.atap: PLN regional rooftop solar quota {mw} MW (RUPTL Table 2.6, 2025-2034); score = percentile.
st.k.risiko: {b} of {n} non-operating projects are in trouble (cancelled, delayed or past COD target), {mwb} of {mw} MW; score = 100 minus the problem MW share.
st.k.dana: {lokal} funded projects recorded in this cell; national funding depth of this technology is at percentile {nas}; score = half national plus half local.
st.kes.kuat: {tek} in {prov} is a strong opportunity (score {skor}), supported by {kuat} and weakest on {lemah}; worth the priority review list.
st.kes.telaah: {tek} in {prov} is worth a closer look (score {skor}): strong on {kuat}, but {lemah} needs checking before moving.
st.kes.terbatas: {tek} in {prov} is still limited (score {skor}); the strongest component is {kuat}, while {lemah} holds the score down.
st.radar.sub: Planned, under-construction and delayed projects with measurable warning signs
st.radar.judul: {hl} of {total} pipeline projects are high risk, representing {mw} MW
st.radar.grafik: Bars of project counts by warning sign
st.radar.catatan: {cod} MW of the {total} MW pipeline is past its COD target. Score = sum of warning points (past COD 3, delayed 3, social issue in project news 3, no developer 2, low system absorption 2, no funder 1, regional social pressure 1); high at 5 or more, medium 3 to 4.
st.radar.pilih: Select a project name in the table to see warning signs and the checklist.
st.radar.bersih: No measurable warning signs in the existing data.
st.radar.kes.tinggi: This project belongs on the priority watch list: several layered warning signs. Verify directly with the developer and PLN before using it as a supply or investment assumption.
st.radar.kes.sedang: Medium risk: warning signs exist but are not layered. Go through the checklist before relying on the project schedule.
st.radar.kes.rendah: Low risk according to the existing data; missing data is not proof of safety.
st.tanda.cod: COD target {cod} passed {lewat} year(s) ago but the project is not yet operating.
st.tanda.pengembang: Owner or developer is unnamed (empty or only an IPP label).
st.tanda.dana: No funder, borrower or funding scheme is recorded for this project.
st.tanda.sosial: {n} news items linked to the project mention social issues (opposition, dispute, compensation, stalled). Example:
st.tanda.sosial_wil: {n} news items on the same technology in {prov} mention social issues.
st.tanda.konflik: {n} news items in {prov} mention conflict or opposition; there is no separate conflict-area register.
st.tanda.serap: The {sistem} system has a {rm} percent reserve margin and the project equals {rasio} percent of net peak load; its ability to absorb added variable renewables is low.
st.periksa.jadwal: Ask the developer or PLN for the latest COD schedule and the cause of delay; check whether the PPA is signed.
st.periksa.pihak: Find the actual owner or developer (AHU, PLN reports, press releases) and record their technical and financial track record.
st.periksa.dana: Ask about the funding sources (equity, loans, DFI) and financial close status.
st.periksa.sosial: Read the linked news, check land acquisition status, community consent and environmental permits.
st.periksa.jaringan: Ask for the interconnection study and the variable renewable absorption limit of the system, and the grid reinforcement plan.
st.hhi.sub: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of operating capacity by owner
st.hhi.judul: {hl} HHI points of ownership in {tek}, classed as {kelas}
st.hhi.grafik: Bars of operating-capacity HHI per technology, dashed line the high-concentration threshold
st.hhi.catatan: HHI = sum of squared shares (percent) of each owner, 0 to 10,000; below 1,500 low, 1,500 to 2,500 moderate, above it high. Only {n} of {total} operating plants have a named owner, so read the coverage column before concluding. Joint owners split evenly.
st.hhi.kes: In {tek}, {nama} holds {pangsa} of capacity with a named owner (data coverage {cakupan}); high concentration means one big player's decision shifts supply.
st.pangsa.sub: Cumulative operating capacity by owner group and actual COD year
st.pangsa.judul: The state-owned share fell from {dari} percent in {a} to {hl} percent in {z}
st.pangsa.grafik: Lines of state-owned, private and foreign shares of renewable capacity with a named owner per year
st.pangsa.catatan: Only operating plants with a named owner and an actual COD year. Groups are inferred from names (PLN, Indonesia Power, PJB, Pertamina, Geo Dipa, Inalum = state-owned; foreign legal entities = foreign; the rest private), so hypothesis.
st.pangsa.kes: The private share of {swasta} and foreign share of {asing} grew from small bases, so renewable supply increasingly depends on IPP contracts; PPA quality and contract risk become the main issue.
st.pemain.sub: Capacity added since 2022 plus pipeline with a named owner
st.pemain.judul: {hl} players added capacity since 2022 or hold a pipeline; the largest is {nama}
st.pemain.grafik: Bars of added capacity plus pipeline for the top eight players
st.pemain.catatan: Added = operating MW with an actual COD of 2022 or later. Growth = added divided by capacity before 2022 (blank without a base). Owner name spellings are merged where needed; unnamed owners are not counted.
st.pemain.kes: {nama} ({gol}) leads on added capacity plus pipeline; large pipeline players without an operating record need their funding readiness assessed.
st.alokasi.sub: Share of public renewable funding against share of RUPTL pipeline MW by technology
st.uang.judul: {tek} holds {mw} of pipeline MW but only {dana} of public funding: reallocation gap {hl}
st.uang.grafik: Dots of pipeline MW share and public funding share per technology
st.uang.catatan: Public renewable funding {a} to {z} (CPI via IRENA, 2023 prices); funding labelled multiple ({camp}) is not allocated. An absolute USD need is not computed because projects with both an investment value and a capacity are too few; what is computed is the reallocation gap if funding followed the MW spread. JETP commits {jetp} (2023 to 2030) and is not split by technology.
st.uang.kes: If public funding followed the pipeline MW spread, about {total} would shift; {tek} is relatively most underfunded. This is an allocation difference, not an absolute investment need.
st.tahunan.sub: International funding commitments (IATI) and public renewable investment per year, USD billion
st.tahunan.judul: International funding commitments recorded at {hl}, peaking in {tahun}, from {n} activities
st.tahunan.grafik: Lines of international commitments and public renewable investment per year in USD billion
st.tahunan.catatan: IATI commitments are weighted by each activity's energy share and recorded in the activity year, not the disbursement year; public investment ends before 2025 because of the source release. The two series must not be added because they can overlap.
st.provdana.sub: Projects with recorded funding by project location
st.provdana.judul: Only {hl} of {total} provinces have projects with recorded funding
st.provdana.catatan: IATI international funding mostly does not name a province, so the provincial breakdown covers only projects linked to METI projects with a clear location. These figures are a lower bound, not a complete funding map.
st.mom.sub: Change in the share of technology-tagged news between two full-month windows
st.mom.grafik: Dots of news share per technology in the earlier and later windows
st.mom.catatan: Earlier window: {a}; later window: {z}. Shares are compared, not counts, so the harvest pace does not bias it. Technologies with fewer than five news items across both windows are not shown. News is harvested automatically and covers only a few months.
st.mom.kes: Media attention is shifting to {tek}; news momentum is not project momentum, but it often precedes tender or policy announcements.
st.bulanan.sub: Technology-tagged news and mentions of key events per month
st.bulanan.judul: Of {hl} news items, {n} mention inauguration, PPA, tender or cancellation; {batal} projects are cancelled or delayed
st.bulanan.grafik: Stacked columns of news counts per month by technology
st.bulanan.catatan: Topics are recognised from title keywords (inauguration, PPA and contracts, tenders, cancelled or delayed), so only indicative. Verified events from official ESDM and PLN news are counted separately in the last column. The latest news is dated {tgl}; the current month is marked partial.
st.metode.sub: Formulas, weights, sources and limitations of each part
st.metode.judul: Every number is computed with fixed formulas from open data; there is no AI model
st.m.kesenjangan.rumus: Mix: trend = linear regression of 2015-2024 realisation; needed per year = (target minus 2024 realisation) divided by remaining years; year reached = 2024 plus gap divided by trend. Capacity: historical pace = (2024 renewable capacity minus 2015) divided by 9; need = MW gap divided by remaining years. Per technology: pace = IRENA capacity difference 2015-2025 divided by 10; need = named RUPTL MW (planned and under construction) divided by 10.
st.m.kesenjangan.batas: KEN targets use primary energy and RUKN uses generation; they are not mixed. The per-technology need is a lower bound because part of the RUPTL target is not itemised. A linear trend does not account for policy jumps.
st.m.peta.rumus: Each province and technology cell is rated on the components below, each normalised to 0 to 100 (percentile across provinces, or a direct value), then averaged with weights over the components that exist. Remaining potential = RUEN/HEESI potential minus installed. Tariff = local BPP divided by (Perpres 112 benchmark tariff at the pipeline median tier x location factor). Pipeline = planned and under-construction RUPTL MW. Rooftop quota = regional rooftop solar quota (solar only). RUED = 100 with a target, 50 without a target, 0 if not recorded. Risk = 100 minus the problem MW share. Funding = half the percentile of national technology funding depth plus half a local funded-project count score. A cell needs at least three components.
st.m.peta.batas: RUEN potential is 2015-based and hydro is by region group; the latest BPP in the file is 2020; the rooftop quota is regional only; mini and micro hydro is hydro up to 10 MW; cells with fewer than three components are not scored.
st.m.radar.rumus: Projects that are planned, under construction or delayed receive points: past COD target 3, delayed 3, linked news mentioning social issues 3, no named developer 2, low system absorption 2 (reserve margin 50 percent or more, or solar and wind projects above 10 percent of net peak load), no recorded funder 1, similar social issue or conflict in the province 1. High at 5 or more, medium 3 to 4.
st.m.radar.batas: Social issues are recognised from keywords in news titles; there is no separate conflict-area register. Missing developer and funder data often means data not yet collected, not a project without owners.
st.m.konsentrasi.rumus: HHI = sum of squared percent shares of each owner over operating MW with a named owner. Group share = cumulative MW by actual COD year. Growing players = MW with an actual COD of 2022 or later plus pipeline MW with a named owner.
st.m.konsentrasi.batas: Many operating plants (especially rooftop solar) do not yet have a named owner; coverage is shown in the table. Owner groups are inferred from names.
st.m.uang.rumus: Public renewable funding over the last ten years by technology (CPI via IRENA, USD at 2023 prices) compared with the RUPTL pipeline MW share. Reallocation gap = (MW share times total funding) minus recorded funding. International commitments per year from IATI are weighted by energy share.
st.m.uang.batas: Not an absolute investment need; cost per MW differs by technology, so the MW share is only a rough comparison. Provinces are filled only for linked projects.
st.m.sinyal.rumus: Technology-tagged news is counted per month. Momentum = technology share in the latest full-month window minus the previous window. Topics are recognised from title keywords. Verified events are counted from official ESDM and PLN news.
st.m.sinyal.batas: News coverage spans only a few months and is harvested automatically, so monthly trends are sensitive to the harvest pace.
st.m.bobot: Weights of the opportunity score components
st.m.celah: Data limitations to be aware of
st.m.celah_konflik: There is no register of conflict areas or land acquisition data; only keywords in news.
st.m.celah_kebutuhan: Absolute investment needs (CIPP, RUPTL) per technology are not in the data; there are too few cost-per-MW samples.
st.m.celah_pemilik: Named owners exist for only part of operating plants; rooftop solar is almost entirely unnamed.
st.m.celah_berita: News has been collected since July 2026; not yet enough for seasonal trends.
st.m.celah_mikro: Mini and micro hydro means hydro up to 10 MW; its installed capacity is not separated from hydro in HEESI.
st.m.celah_atap: The rooftop solar quota exists only for four PLN regions, not per province or UP3.
st.m.katalog: All sources of each part are under the info icon in that part's header; the complete dataset list is in the source catalogue (public/data/sumber_katalog.json).
st.m.ulang: Computation runs in the browser from the same data files so results are repeatable; the code is in strategi_hitung.js and tested with reference numbers in tests/strategi.test.mjs.

rd2.metode.rumus: Score = sum of (weight x norm 0 to 1) over the available components, times 100. Norm = min-max across 38 provinces (gaps and regency footprint use log(1 + x)). Components without data are left out and weights recomputed; at least five components (all technologies) or four (one technology); new provinces whose potential is not yet split from the parent province are not scored. All weights are hypotheses, not market forecasts.

rd2.celah.1: A regency-level map is not possible yet: the repository has no regency geometry or coordinates. The map shows provinces (average regency score) and the table lists all 514 regencies and cities.
rd2.celah.2: Wind speed and grid or substations per regency are not in the score: there is no wind raster and no substation point that can be placed in a regency without polygons.
rd2.celah.3: Resource, BPP, benchmark price and village access are identical for all regencies in a province (inherited). Only projects, EIA and regulations tell regencies apart, and only where the name matches the data.
rd2.celah.4: RUEN potential dates from 2015 and the latest BPP in the file is the 2020 BPP.

rd2.d.prio.cara: Weighted average, each component min-max across provinces; empty components are left out and weights recomputed. Hypothesis.
rd2.d.r1: Energy replaced (kWh) = annual diesel generation (GWh) x 1 million x share replaced.
rd2.d.r2: Diesel saved (liters) = energy replaced x specific consumption (liters per kWh).
rd2.d.r3: Fuel saving (Rp) = diesel saved x latest Dexlite price.
rd2.d.r4: Solar plus battery cost (Rp) = energy replaced x cost (US cents per kWh) x exchange rate.
rd2.d.r5: Net saving = fuel saving minus solar plus battery cost.
rd2.d.r6: Solar needed (MWp) = energy replaced / (province PVOUT x system efficiency 0.8) / 1000.
rd2.d.celah.1: Diesel capacity and generation exist only per province (2024 Electricity Statistics); isolated systems only have BPP (2020 decree).
rd2.d.celah.2: PLN statistics per system and RUPTL per island are not reachable, so island-level figures are missing.
rd2.d.celah.3: Solar plus battery cost, specific consumption, exchange rate and efficiency are hypothesized assumptions; diesel price uses Jabodetabek Dexlite as a benchmark, not PLN's purchase price.
rd2.d.celah.4: The replaced share is uniform across each province's systems; battery needs (MWh) are not computed.

kr2.n.ppa: Curated from news and company announcements; not the whole market. An empty capacity means the source does not state it.
kr2.celah.1: SBTi and RE100 list only the headquarters country, not where a company operates: foreign companies appear only when a sourced renewable purchase in Indonesia exists and they are in one of the registries.
kr2.celah.2: The PPA and REC list is curated from news and company announcements; corporate contracts are rarely announced, so it is not the whole market. Scheme, price, and term are left out when the source does not give them.
kr2.celah.3: SBTi and RE100 target wording is not copied; read it at the source. Withdrawn means the company did not submit a target within 24 months.
kr2.celah.4: Companies not yet in the directory show a monogram instead of a logo.
kr2.agr.xurya-200: Xurya rooftop solar portfolio, over 300 projects
kn2.title: Plant performance | METI Directory
kn2.deskripsi: Actual capacity factors of power plants by technology and province, compared with the RUPTL plan reference, with sources and dates.
kn2.lead: How much power plants actually deliver compared with what they could deliver all year: 2024 capacity factors by technology and province, against the RUPTL plan reference.
kn2.s.tek: Actual 2024 capacity factor = output / (capacity x 8,760 hours)
kn2.n.tek: The national capacity factor uses 2024 PLN output divided by PLN system capacity (RUPTL, October 2024). The lower bound uses capacity of all operators (ESDM), including captive plants whose output is not in PLN figures. Plan reference = RUPTL 2025 planned energy divided by 2024 capacity, only for types whose fleet is fairly stable.
kn2.s.wil: Provinces with at least {mw} MW of this type; lower bound because capacity covers all operators
kn2.n.wil: Output is PLN only (including leased and IPP purchases) while capacity covers all operators: provincial figures are lower bounds, especially for solar and bioenergy. Per-plant data is not available.
kn2.t.wil_kosong: No province has enough {tek} capacity to compare
kn2.s.ekstrem: Top and bottom five provinces, at least {mw} MW of capacity
kn2.eks.sedikit: Too few provinces have {tek} capacity to rank.
kn2.celah.1: Per-unit or per-plant output is not in the repo data, so the finest level is plant type by province, not per unit.
kn2.celah.2: ESDM 2024 output is PLN only while ESDM capacity covers all operators: provincial capacity factors are lower bounds, especially solar and biomass.
kn2.celah.3: The national capacity factor uses PLN system capacity from RUPTL (October 2024, excluding Batam) and full-year output that includes Batam, so it stays an estimate.
kn2.celah.4: The plan reference is computed only for coal, gas, hydro, and geothermal; solar, wind, biomass, and diesel are left blank because capacity grows fast or the scope differs.
kn2.celah.5: IRENA capacity factor assumptions and issuer reports are not in the data; RUPTL gives no capacity factor figures by type.
kn2.celah.6: Output above capacity (West Kalimantan hydro, likely imported power) is flagged as an anomaly and not computed.
kn2.celah.7: PLTGB and other plants in ESDM capacity are not mapped to any type.
kn2.alasan.bbm: Planned oil-fuel energy covers more than diesel plants
kn2.alasan.tumbuh: Capacity grows fast, plan not comparable
kn2.alasan.cakupan: RUPTL capacity scope differs from ESDM

hk2.deskripsi: Prices of solar modules, Li-ion batteries and wind turbines over time, plus Indonesia's RE component exports and imports by HS code and country of origin, with sources and dates.
hk2.lead: Prices of solar modules, Li-ion batteries and wind turbines over time, plus Indonesia's RE component exports and imports by HS code and country of origin.
hk2.kosong: No recorded trade for this component, direction and year.
hk2.b.modul: Nominal USD per watt; since 2010 it uses the European market benchmark (pvXchange), not Indonesian import prices.
hk2.b.tic-surya: Real 2024 USD per kW DC, global weighted average (IRENA).
hk2.b.modul-eropa-2024: 2024 USD per watt, pvXchange via IRENA.
hk2.b.pack: Volume-weighted average across segments, real dollars of each survey year (BNEF); 2022 is omitted because sources disagree.
hk2.b.sistem-baterai: Real 2024 USD per kWh, installed and commissioned battery storage projects (IRENA from BNEF).
hk2.b.turnkey-2024: 2024 USD per kWh, turnkey system excluding EPC and grid connection.
hk2.b.tic-bayu: Real 2024 USD per kW, turbine plus balance of project, global weighted average (IRENA).
hk2.b.turbin-tiongkok: 2024 USD per kW; contracts in China often exclude delivery, installation and towers.
hk2.t.harga: Solar module prices fell {hl} from {a} to {b}, with batteries and turbines following
hk2.t.dampak: Modules account for {hl} of the fall in solar PV installed cost {a} to {b} ({p}%)
hk2.t.neraca: Indonesia imported RE components worth {hl} in {tahun}, with exports of {e} million USD
hk2.t.dagang: Indonesia's trade in {hl} year by year
hk2.t.negara: Indonesia's trading partners for {hl} by country
hk2.s.harga: Global prices over time; every point has a source, evidence level and date
hk2.s.dampak: Fall in utility-scale solar PV installed cost by component, USD per kW; global LCOE fell from {l0} to {l1} US cents/kWh
hk2.s.dagang: Values in million USD per UN Comtrade
hk2.n.harga: Dollar basis differs between sources (nominal or real, different years); read the basis under each series before comparing.
hk2.n.dampak: Simple estimate: each component's share of the installed cost decline multiplied by the global LCOE decline, assuming LCOE moves in line with capital cost. Capacity factor and financing cost are not separated.
hk2.n.neraca: Balance = exports minus imports; negative means Indonesia is a net importer. 6-digit HS codes include non-RE goods, see Data gaps.
hk2.n.surya: The solar series breaks in 2022: through 2021 it uses HS 8541.40 (which also covers LEDs and diodes), from 2022 HS 8541.43 (cells assembled into modules).
hk2.tren.j: Imports and exports of {k} by year
hk2.inv.kartu: {p}% of the fall in solar PV installed cost {a} to {b}
hk2.inv.n: No open time series of inverter prices exists; only the inverter's contribution to the solar PV cost decline is available (IRENA).
hk2.celah.1: There is no open time series of inverter prices. Only the inverter's contribution to the 2010 to 2024 fall in solar installed cost is available (IRENA); pvXchange or InfoLink inverter price series and the full BNEF survey are paywalled or may not be redistributed.
hk2.celah.2: BNEF battery pack prices for 2022 are omitted: secondary sources quote both 151 and 161 USD per kWh (different dollar bases). Each BNEF point uses real dollars of its own survey year, so year-on-year change is only computed when the previous year exists.
hk2.celah.3: Wind turbine prices over time are only published as charts in the IRENA report; what can be quoted is onshore wind installed cost per year (turbine plus balance of project) and 2024 turbine prices inside and outside China.
hk2.celah.4: Module prices from 2010 are the European market benchmark (pvXchange), not Indonesian import prices; Indonesian import values are in the trade section.
hk2.celah.5: The LCOE impact is a simple estimate (EST): share of the installed cost decline multiplied by the global LCOE decline, assuming LCOE moves in line with capital cost; capacity factor and financing cost are not accounted for.
hk2.dcelah.1: Trade data comes from UN Comtrade (as reported by Indonesia at 6-digit HS), not the 8-digit BPS tables; values follow Comtrade reporting and may be revised.
hk2.dcelah.2: The solar series breaks in 2022: through 2021 it uses HS 8541.40 (cells, modules, and also LEDs and diodes), from 2022 HS 8541.43 (cells assembled into modules). Do not compare 2021 with 2022 directly.
hk2.dcelah.3: HS 8502.31 (wind-powered generating sets) and 8504.40 (static converters, including chargers and UPS, not only solar inverters) include non-RE goods; HS 8507.60 covers all lithium-ion batteries, including vehicles and electronics.
hk2.dcelah.4: Origin and destination use the partner country as reported by Indonesia; transit and cross-border assembly are not visible. Only the 25 largest partners per year are included.
hk2.dcelah.5: 2025 data is not included yet; Comtrade is only complete after annual reports are filed.

pz2.k.oss.kosong: OSS service and actual permit-time data are not published openly; the component is left out.
pz2.metode.judul: Five components, fixed weights, empty components left out
pz2.metode.tanggal: Data built {tanggal}. Hypothesis: not an official ease-of-doing-business measure.
pz2.m.rued: 100 with a RUED bylaw that has a numeric target, 60 with a bylaw without one, 0 when not recorded.
pz2.m.perda: Number of supporting provincial bylaws divided by the highest count across provinces, times 100. RUED is not counted twice.
pz2.m.wkp: 100 with a WKP being tendered, 80 if producing or being developed, 50 if only under study. Left out when there is no WKP.
pz2.m.berita: 100 minus 40 points per permit-problem news item naming the province. Left out when there is none.
pz2.m.oss: OSS and local one-stop service data and actual permit times are not available; left out for every province.
pz2.celah.1: Actual average permit time is not public data; only 3 AMDAL-to-COD pairs exist on the permits and contracts page, too few to use.
pz2.celah.2: Local OSS and one-stop service data have not been collected; the component is left out everywhere.
pz2.celah.3: RUED and bylaws are counted from files recorded in the repository; a province without a record may still have bylaws.
pz2.celah.4: Permit-problem news is matched by headline (the word permit plus a province name) and the count is small.

kd2.kh.lead: National outage trend, reserve margin of each PLN system to 2034, network losses and the systems that need storage. Per-UID figures are not openly published.
kd2.tren.judul: Outage time is down {a}% since 2020, now {v} hours per customer
kd2.tren.sub: PLN SAIDI, SAIFI and network losses
kd2.tren.narasi: SAIDI is the average outage time per customer in a year and SAIFI the average number of outages. Figures per PLN region or UID are not published as open files, so the national series is shown.
kd2.tren.cat: 2015 to 2019 from the 2025-2034 RUPTL (Table 4.51), 2020 to 2024 from the 2024 Electricity Statistics (Table 47). The RUPTL shows 4.5 hours and 2.7 outages for 2024 through October; the Statistics book covers the full year.
kd2.peta.sub: Reserve margin per system, RUPTL 2025-2034 RE Base scenario
kd2.peta.narasi: Reserve margin is the surplus of dependable capacity over peak load. Provinces in one system share a colour. Pick a measure below, hover for values, click for system details.
kd2.peta.label: Map of PLN system reserve margin by province

kd2.sorot.sub: Lowest reserve {rm}% or less and renewables {ebt}% or more of 2034 peak load (Hypothesis)
kd2.sorot.isi: Lowest reserve {rm}%, renewables {ebt}% of 2034 peak load. Storage in the RUPTL: {mw} MW.
kd2.sorot.cat: Hypothesis: the 35% reserve and 50% renewable thresholds are the authors' choice. Renewables in the RUPTL balance include hydro and geothermal, not only solar and wind, so real storage needs require a system study.
kd2.tabel.judul: {n} PLN systems in the RUPTL power balance
kd2.tabel.sub: Peak load, reserve margin, renewables and storage
kd2.tabel.label: Power balance per PLN system
kd2.dlg.simpan: Battery and pumped storage in the RUPTL project list for this system's provinces: {mw} MW (power balance Table {tabel}).
kd2.dlg.catatan: Source: PLN RUPTL 2025-2034, RE Base scenario. The system-to-province mapping follows the RUPTL text and the authors' estimate (Hypothesis).
kd2.metode.judul: What is available, what is not published
kd2.metode.isi: The national trend and the power balances are read directly from official documents. What the documents do not contain is left empty and not invented.
kd2.celah.1: SAIDI and SAIFI per PLN region or UID are not published as open files (the ESDM Statistics and the RUPTL are national only; the PLN Statistics site could not be reached from the harvest environment).
kd2.celah.2: Renewable curtailment: no sourced figure exists, so none is shown.
kd2.celah.3: The system-to-province mapping follows the RUPTL text; Central Sulawesi is only partly in Sulbagut and the Riau Islands (Batam system) has no balance.
kd2.celah.4: Renewables in the power balance include hydro and geothermal, not only variable sources, so the storage flag is a Hypothesis.

mk.cara1: Energy in year t = capacity kW x 8,760 hours x capacity factor x (1 - degradation)^(t-1). Revenue = energy x paid share x year-t tariff, plus REC and carbon.
mk.cara2: EBITDA = revenue - opex (fixed opex + roof lease + major replacement, escalating). Year 0 capex = kW x capex per kW x exchange rate, plus VAT unless borne by government.
mk.cara3: Annuity debt: payment = D x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n). Tax = rate x (EBITDA - depreciation - interest), losses carried forward, a tax holiday exempts early years. DSCR = (EBITDA - tax) / payment.
mk.cara4: IRR is found by bisection until NPV is zero; NPV uses the discount rate; payback is interpolated where cumulative cash flow crosses zero; LCOE = (capex + PV of opex) / PV of energy.
mk.cara5: Simplifications: all capex in year 0 with no interest during construction, straight-line depreciation, tax losses carried forward without limit, no working capital or residual value. All results are Hypotheses.

mk.m.l1: Energy in year t = capacity kW x 8,760 hours x capacity factor x (1 - degradation)^(t-1). Revenue = energy x paid share x year-t tariff, plus REC and carbon.
mk.m.l2: EBITDA = revenue - opex (fixed opex + roof lease + major replacement, escalating). Year 0 capex = kW x capex per kW x exchange rate, plus VAT unless borne by government.
mk.m.l3: Annuity debt: payment = D x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n). Tax = rate x (EBITDA - depreciation - interest), losses carried forward, a tax holiday exempts early years. DSCR = (EBITDA - tax) / payment.
mk.m.l4: IRR is found by bisection until NPV is zero; NPV uses the discount rate; payback is interpolated where cumulative cash flow crosses zero; LCOE = (capex + PV of opex) / PV of energy.
mk.m.f1: IRR: NPV(r) = Σ flow_t / (1 + r)^t = 0, t = 0..life
mk.m.f2: DSCR_t = (EBITDA_t - tax_t) / payment_t ; LCOE = (capex + Σ opex_t/(1+d)^t) / Σ energy_t/(1+d)^t
mk.m.b1: Simplifications: all capex in year 0 with no interest during construction, straight-line depreciation, tax losses carried forward without limit, no working capital or residual value. All results are Hypotheses.
mk.m.b2: Defaults without a source are left empty. Capital structure (debt, interest, tenor) has no official reference so the user supplies it.

sp2.metode.sub: Gaps are written plainly, not filled with guesses
sp2.metode.tanggal: Assembled {tanggal} from this repository's public files.
sp2.celah.1: Network losses are published only nationally (transmission and distribution), not per system: per-system losses are left empty.
sp2.celah.2: Per-system generation cost under the latest ministerial decree was not found as an open file; the last readable value is 2020. The national RUPTL 2025 figure of Rp 1,829/kWh comes from the RUPTL FAQ.
sp2.celah.3: Peak load and reserve margin per system come only from the 2025-2034 RUPTL power balance (projection, not actuals); Sumbagut and Sumbagselteng share one Sumatra-Bangka table so load is not split.
sp2.celah.4: Nusa Tenggara, Maluku and Papua are sets of separate (isolated) systems: loads are summed and reserve margin takes the lowest subsystem value each year. RUPTL projects whose tables carry no province (including all of Papua) are not counted in the RUPTL rows.
sp2.celah.5: Installed capacity covers all operators (PLN, non-PLN and captive) in 2024; output covers PLN only including leased and purchased IPP power.
sp2.celah.6: Penetration limits, curtailment and new demand (research from RUPTL 2025-2034 Annex E.1-E.2, IEA, Tumiran): penetration limits are study results, the only curtailment figure is an IEA model (not a measured event), and Sulawesi, Maluku, Papua and Nusa Tenggara are not yet parsed from Annex E.3, so 0 items does not mean no demand.
sp2.celah.7: Interconnection COD dates are not in any openly readable source: left empty.
