cl.title: Location check | METI Directory
cl.judul: How suitable is one point for a renewable project?
cl.lead: Click the map or enter coordinates. Everything is computed in your browser from static files: region, solar potential, grid distance, land status, hazard, cost of supply (BPP) and nearest projects. The score is labelled Hypothesis, not a feasibility study.
ky.title: Renewable business confidence index | METI Directory
ky.judul: How confident are renewable energy businesses this quarter?
ky.lead: Answer eight short questions once per quarter. Results appear only as aggregates when at least five accounts have answered, with no names and no individual answers.
ad.title: METI Academy | METI Directory
ad.judul: Learn renewable energy step by step
ad.lead: Six short modules that string together the topics, glossary and methods of this wiki into an ordered learning path. Each module ends with a multiple-choice quiz from sourced content. Badges mark participation and are not official certificates.
cl.deskripsi: Click the map or enter coordinates: region, solar potential, distance to substations and transmission, land status, hazard, BPP, nearest projects and a short feasibility score labelled Hypothesis.
ky.deskripsi: Quarterly renewable business confidence survey for members: eight items, index per item and trend, shown only with at least five respondents.
ad.deskripsi: A short renewable energy learning path: basics, rooftop solar, licensing, finance, carbon and safety, with sourced multiple-choice quizzes and participation badges.
cl.cara: Everything is computed in your browser from static files; coordinates are not sent to a server.
cl.cara.label: How it is computed
cl.s.pilih: The point must be in Indonesia. A negative latitude means south of the equator.
cl.f.salah: Invalid coordinates. Enter latitude -11.5 to 6.5 and longitude 94.5 to 141.5.
cl.peta.label: Point picker map. Click to choose a location.
cl.peta.ajak: Click the map to choose a point. Results appear below.
cl.peta.galat: The map could not be loaded. Enter coordinates manually.
cl.kosong: No point yet. Click the map or enter coordinates and the per-aspect results and short score appear here.
cl.luar: This point is outside any province boundary in our data (possibly sea or abroad). Pick a point on Indonesian land.
cl.t.metode: {hl} score components, all of them Hypothesis
cl.s.metode: Weights and thresholds are METI assumptions for first screening. Components without data are dropped and the remaining weights rescaled; a score appears only with at least three components.
cl.rumus.sumber: Provincial PVOUT (kWh/kWp per year): 1,200 scores 0, 1,650 scores 100, linear in between.
cl.rumus.jaringan: Distance to the nearest substation or line of 150 kV and up: 5 km or less scores 100, 50 km or more scores 0, linear in between.
cl.rumus.lahan: 100 minus the deduction of each class covering the point: protected, conservation, mangrove 100 (closed); peat and customary 50; HTI and HPH 35; palm oil 30; production 25; conversion 10.
cl.rumus.bahaya: 100 minus the InaRISK multi-hazard index (0 to 100) read from the map pixel colour.
cl.rumus.bpp: Percentile of the provincial system BPP among provinces with data: a high BPP means renewables compete more easily.
cl.celah.1: Solar potential is one point per province (the capital), not the value at your location; wind is unavailable because no open per-region summary exists.
cl.celah.2: Substations and lines come from OpenStreetMap (volunteer, unofficial) and cover only four coordinate boxes: Java, Bali, parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan. Elsewhere the grid component is dropped.
cl.celah.3: Land status uses simplified polygons (KLHK 2017, GFW concessions 2021, mangrove 2016): estimates, not legal boundaries. The customary land map is incomplete, so a clear result does not mean claim-free.
cl.celah.4: Hazard is read from one InaRISK image layer at about 4 km resolution: a relative indication, not a risk assessment.
cl.celah.5: The regency is not detected automatically because regency boundaries are not in the repo; choose one to see its Radar score.
cl.galat.data: Some data files could not be loaded. Reload the page.
cl.kab.catatan: A regency Radar score inherits resource, BPP and access from its province.
cl.tanpa_data: No data yet for this province.
cl.catatan.atlas: Value at the provincial capital (Global Solar Atlas): a relative indication, not the value at your point.
cl.catatan.osm: Source OpenStreetMap, volunteer and unofficial; not PLN data.
cl.catatan.bpp: BPP per system under Energy Ministry Decree 2020. The Presidential Reg. 112/2022 location factor applies to benchmark prices and is not multiplied here.
cl.jaringan.luar: This point is outside the harvested substation and line boxes, so the distances below are unreliable and the grid component is excluded from the score.
cl.lahan.bersih: No sensitive land class in our data at this point.
cl.bahaya.tanpa: No hazard data at this point.
cl.t.skor0: The score cannot be computed yet
cl.s.skor0: Fewer than three components have data at this point.
cl.s.skor: Computed from the components available; weight used {p} of 100.
cl.grafik.label: Score per component, 0 to 100
cl.skor.peringatan: A first-screening hypothesis: not a feasibility study, and no substitute for field survey, land assessment or permits.
cl.s.hasil: Province {prov}. Estimates from static files, not survey data.
cl.m.l1: Pick a point on the map or enter coordinates; the point must lie in the Indonesia box.
cl.m.l2: The province is found by a point-in-polygon test on province boundaries; the BPS code comes from that boundary.
cl.m.l3: Distances to substations and lines are computed in the browser (haversine and point-to-segment); land status by point-in-polygon tests on five layers.
cl.m.l4: Hazard is read from the InaRISK image pixel colour: green maps to index 0, red to index 1.
cl.m.l5: Each component is scored 0 to 100 and weighted; components without data are dropped.
cl.m.r1: score = sum(weight x component score) / sum(weights of components present)
cl.m.r2: weights: resource 25, grid 25, land 25, hazard 15, BPP 10 (Hypothesis); at least 3 components
cl.m.b1: Weights and thresholds are METI assumptions (Hypothesis), not yet calibrated against operating projects.
cl.m.b2: Grid, land and hazard data are estimates from static files; check official sources before any investment decision.
met.h.cek-lokasi.j: Location check: short feasibility score for one point
met.h.cek-lokasi.s: Global Solar Atlas, OpenStreetMap, KLHK, GFW, InaRISK, Energy Ministry Decree 2020; all weights Hypothesis
ky.s.survei: Eight items on a 1 to 5 scale. Your answer is stored once per quarter and can be changed until the quarter ends.
ky.s.survei.ubah: You have already answered this quarter. You may change your answers until the quarter ends.
ky.q.kondisi: How positive is your view of renewable business conditions compared with three months ago?
ky.q.pipeline: How positive is the outlook for the projects in your pipeline over the next three months?
ky.q.pembiayaan: How easy is it to obtain financing or capital now?
ky.q.perizinan: How smooth is the licensing process you face?
ky.q.harga: How adequate are the electricity prices or tariffs you can obtain?
ky.q.regulasi: How certain are renewable regulations and policies for your plans?
ky.q.investasi: How positive are your investment plans for the next 12 months?
ky.q.tenaga: How positive are your workforce plans for the next 12 months?
ky.privasi: Answers are never shown per person. Aggregates appear only when at least {n} accounts answered in the same quarter.
ky.t.indeks0: The index is not shown yet
ky.s.indeks: Normalised average 0 to 100; 50 means neutral. Only quarters with enough respondents are shown.
ky.tutup: Only {n} accounts have answered. Results appear once at least {m} accounts answer in the same quarter (privacy).
ky.tutup_ini: This quarter has only {n} respondents (minimum {m}); the latest quarter with enough is shown.
ky.s.tren: Only quarters with at least five respondents; two or more quarters are needed.
ky.tren0: The trend appears once two quarters meet the respondent minimum.
ky.s.metode: A simple index that can be recomputed from the answers.
ky.m.1: Each item score (1 to 5) is averaged across respondents in a quarter, then item index = (average minus 1) times 25: 1 becomes 0, 3 becomes 50 (neutral), 5 becomes 100.
ky.m.2: The combined index is the average of the eight item indices with equal weights (Hypothesis).
ky.m.3: One account gives one answer per quarter; the server sets the quarter by WIB time, and past quarters cannot be changed.
ky.m.4: Aggregates are hidden with fewer than five respondents; no name or individual answer is ever shown.
ky.belum_aktif: The survey is not active yet: the database migration has not been run.
met.h.indeks-keyakinan.j: Renewable business confidence index: quarterly survey
met.h.indeks-keyakinan.s: Member account answers; aggregates only with at least five respondents; equal item weights (Hypothesis)
ad.s.jalur: Work in order: open each step (a link to a wiki page), tick it once read, then take the quiz. The suggested module is marked.
ad.s.skor: You pass with a score of at least {n} percent.
ad.grafik.label: Best quiz score per module
ad.penafian: These badges mark participation on the METI platform. They are not an official certificate or competence certification and are not recognised by any certification body.
ad.reset.tanya: Delete all learning progress in this browser?
ad.lokal: Progress is stored only in this browser and is not sent to a server.
ad.c.1: Each module strings together topics, glossary entries, methods and data pages already in this wiki.
ad.c.2: Tick a step once read; the quiz opens when every step is ticked.
ad.c.3: Multiple-choice questions come from sourced topic summaries, the glossary and licensing Q&A; each question links to its source.
ad.c.4: Your best score is kept in this browser; a badge is earned at a score of at least {n} percent.
ad.kuis.petunjuk: Choose one answer per question. You pass with at least {n} percent correct.
ad.lulus: Well done, you passed this module and earned its badge.
ad.belum_lulus: Below {n} percent. Reread the sources, then try again.

rg3.title: Global RE supply chain | METI Directory
rg3.deskripsi: Hub for the global renewable energy supply chain: suppliers, products, world versus Indonesian prices, logistics and landed cost, trade policy, factories worldwide, risks, and WTE and PSEL, each with evidence level and source.
rg3.lead: From factories worldwide to project sites in Indonesia: {n} suppliers from {m} countries and {p} products you can compare. Every figure carries an evidence label and a source; an empty cell means not yet sourced, not zero.
rg3.lead_kosong: Global supply chain data is not available yet. This page reads its data files when opened and will fill in once they are published.
rg3.kosong_semua: No global supply chain data files could be read yet. Try reloading the page later.
rg3.map.gagal: The map could not be loaded.
rg3.map.label: Interactive map
rg3.p.s.neg: Listed suppliers per home country, split by technology. This counts entities, not market share.
rg3.p.j.daftar: Find suppliers by technology, segment, and country
rg3.p.s.daftar: Logos and flags follow source data; names with an organization page link to its profile.
rg3.p.kosong_data: The supplier files are not available yet or are still empty.
rg3.pr.s.katalog: Specifications come from manufacturer datasheets; an empty cell means not yet read from the source, not zero.

rg3.pr.pilih: Pick at least two products from the catalog with the Compare button.
rg3.pr.min: Pick one more product from the same category to start comparing.
rg3.pr.n.banding: Only numeric columns from the comparison schema are scored. Products of different categories cannot be compared.
rg3.pr.s.sert: Recognitions such as Kiwa PVEL Top Performer. Many come from the manufacturer's own press release and are labelled accordingly.
rg3.pr.j.tren: Cell technology share, module efficiency, and laboratory records
rg3.pr.s.tren: An asterisk marks a projection, not measured data.
rg3.pr.n.tren: Two ITRPV editions cannot always be joined into one series; read the year and edition in the tooltip.
rg3.pr.s.pj: Warranty, spare parts, and recycling services where a source exists.
rg3.h.j.bench: {n} components have world prices, {m} have an Indonesian comparison
rg3.h.s.bench: Dated market quotes; exchange rate of {tgl}. Rupiah is a conversion, not a quote.
rg3.h.tanpa_id: No sourced Indonesian price exists for this component yet.
rg3.h.sel_teks: Indonesian prices sit {a}% to {b}% above the first world reference price.
rg3.h.sel_cara: Gap = (Indonesian price - reference world price) / reference world price; not a like-for-like comparison (year, basis, and scope may differ).
rg3.h.n.bench: Reference rate Rp {kurs} per US$. Prices exclude freight, insurance, and taxes unless the market column says otherwise.
rg3.h.kosong_data: The price benchmark file is not available yet or is still empty.
rg3.h.j.id: Price gap for components with an Indonesian comparison
rg3.h.s.id: Only components with both a sourced world price and a sourced Indonesian price are shown.
rg3.h.n.id: Installed cost and component price are not the same thing. This gap is a directional signal, not proof of markup.
rg3.h.j.tren: Component price series from historical sources
rg3.h.s.tren: A logarithmic axis is used when the range exceeds twenty times.
rg3.h.j.bahan: Main raw material prices, first year indexed to 100
rg3.h.s.bahan: World Bank Pink Sheet annual data, nominal USD. The index is made by METI so commodities with different units can be compared.
rg3.h.n.bahan: The index is derived (EST): that year's price divided by the first year's price times 100.
rg3.h.perak_teks: At {mg} mg per watt, silver equals {p}% of the 2025 module price.
rg3.l.s.alur: The duration of each stage appears only when sourced; the rest are marked not yet sourced.
rg3.l.n.alur: The stage order is a general framework for component imports, not the schedule of any specific project.
rg3.l.tahap.po-incoterms.u: The contract sets Incoterms; FOB means the buyer bears freight and insurance.
rg3.l.tahap.produksi.u: The manufacturer builds the components and an inspector checks them before shipment.
rg3.l.tahap.pengapalan.u: Containers are loaded at the origin port and handed to the shipping line.
rg3.l.tahap.layar.u: The ship sails to an Indonesian port; berthing and queue time are not included.
rg3.l.tahap.bea-cukai.u: Import notification, import duty, VAT, and income tax article 22 are paid before release.
rg3.l.tahap.darat-antarpulau.u: Goods move to the project site by road and inter-island sea transport.
rg3.l.s.rute: Pick an origin port to highlight its routes. Distance is a straight line, not a ship track.
rg3.l.n.rute: Sailing days = straight-line distance divided by a speed of 14 knots. This is a lower bound, without queueing, berthing, or transshipment.
rg3.l.j.kalk: From FOB price to rupiah per unit in Indonesia
rg3.l.s.kalk: FOB + freight + insurance + import duty per HS + VAT + income tax article 22. Change the inputs to see the effect.
rg3.l.n.kalk: The result is an estimate (EST). Load per container and insurance are hypotheses you can change; freight uses a global composite index, not a route rate. VAT and income tax article 22 are generally creditable.
rg3.l.f.fm_k: Leave empty to use the reference price.
rg3.l.f.mu_k: A rough hypothesis; change it to match the actual packing.
rg3.l.f.bm_pref: HS {hs}: preferential rate under {p} (needs a certificate of origin).
rg3.l.f.bm_mfn: HS {hs}: MFN rate. A preferential rate may be lower.
rg3.l.f.bm_kosong: HS {hs}: rate not read yet, enter it yourself.
rg3.l.f.lo_k: No sourced data yet; default is zero.
rg3.l.f.api: Importer holds an API (income tax art. 22 at 2.5 percent; 7.5 percent without)
rg3.l.k.rute: {a} to {b}: straight-line distance {km} km, about {hr} sailing days.
rg3.l.k.rute_kosong: This origin country has no reference port in the data; nearest entry port: {b}.
rg3.l.k.tak_lengkap: Price or exchange rate data is incomplete for this calculation.
rg3.l.k.bm_kosong: The import duty rate has not been read for this HS. Fill in the duty field to continue.
rg3.l.k.cara_angkut: Container rate divided by load per container (hypothesis).
rg3.l.k.cara_lokal: Your input; no sourced data yet.
rg3.l.k.cara_mfn: MFN rate from the tariff schedule (BTKI) per HS.
rg3.l.k.cara_pref: Trade agreement preferential rate from an aggregator; not yet checked against official documents.
rg3.l.k.cara_total: Total = CIF + import duty + VAT + income tax art. 22 + inland logistics; VAT and income tax art. 22 apply to CIF + import duty.
rg3.l.kosong_data: The logistics or price benchmark file is not available yet.
rg3.k.s.kd: Anti-dumping duties, tariffs, forced labour bans, and incentives touching the solar supply chain.
rg3.k.kosong_data: The trade policy, trade agreement, and simulation files are not available yet.
rg3.k.dampak: In {th}, Indonesian solar module exports to the US were worth US$ {as} million, {p}% of module exports. Companies affected: {n}.
rg3.k.j.pj: MFN and preferential import duty rates for {n} HS codes
rg3.k.s.pj: Preferences only apply with a certificate of origin from a member country. Faded cells have not been checked against official documents.
rg3.k.tak_repr: This row does not represent a renewable energy component.
rg3.k.n.pj: Preferential rates are used only when checked; otherwise the MFN rate serves as an upper bound.
rg3.k.j.sim: Effect of module and inverter TKDN requirements on cost, supply, and IRR
rg3.k.s.sim: Pick a requirement or click a heat map cell. All results are hypotheses from open assumptions, not price forecasts.
rg3.k.s.capex_patuh: Installed cost if all is bought locally (Rp/kWp)
rg3.k.s.capex_campur: Installed cost if only part is local (Rp/kWp)
rg3.k.s.irr: Project IRR change, all local (percentage points)
rg3.k.s.cakupan: Module demand local factories can meet
rg3.k.s.cara_capex: Base cost + local price premium rising linearly with TKDN, times the import price.
rg3.k.s.cara_campur: Only the share local factories can supply pays the premium; the rest is imported.
rg3.k.s.cara_irr: IRR from the METI financial model with the new installed cost.
rg3.k.s.cara_pasokan: Local capacity passing the requirement divided by annual demand; factories weighted equally.
rg3.k.s.peta: Heat map of project IRR change (percentage points)
rg3.k.s.n_peta: Darker means a bigger IRR drop. Columns are inverter requirements, rows are module requirements.
rg3.k.n.sim: Freight, VAT, income tax art. 22, and incentives are not modelled in this simulation; the local price premium is only a media range.
rg3.pb.s.peta: Flag bubbles count factories per country; factory pins appear where the city coordinates are known.
rg3.pb.n.peta: Coordinates are city or district centres, and country centres for the bubbles; not factory gates.
rg3.pb.j.asean: Indonesia: {m} GW of modules from {n} producers per ministry briefing
rg3.pb.s.asean: Snapshot of {per}, GW per year. It changes quickly; use it as a rough picture.
rg3.pb.s.daftar: Capacities use different units (tons, GW, GWh); do not add them across segments.
rg3.pb.j.neraca: Demand versus local capacity for {n} components
rg3.pb.s.neraca: Demand from the RUPTL pipeline per COD year; gap = demand minus local factory capacity.
rg3.pb.tak_terbaca: Local factory capacity could not be read; the gap is not computed.
rg3.pb.validasi: Validation: imports under HS {hs} in {th} are recorded at US$ {usd} million in UN Comtrade.
rg3.pb.n.neraca: Conversion factors from generation MW to components are entirely hypotheses; there is no official standard.
rg3.pb.kosong_data: The world factory and supply balance files are not available yet.
rg3.r.j.negara: Where Indonesia's component imports come from

rg3.r.cara_pangsa: Partner import value divided by total imports that year.
rg3.r.cara_hhi: HHI = sum of squared percentage shares of all partners (0 to 10,000).
rg3.r.kosong_dagang: Import data for this component is not available yet.
rg3.r.n.negara: Import shares are derived (EST) from official values; Comtrade values may be revised.
rg3.r.j.hhi: Which segments are centred on one country
rg3.r.s.hhi: HHI of listed suppliers per home country. The higher it is, the fewer countries dominate the segment.
rg3.r.n.hhi: This counts listed entities, not market share or capacity. A hypothesis, not a market measure.
rg3.r.j.esg: Forced labour ban rules and supplier issues
rg3.r.s.esg: The US UFLPA and the EU forced labour regulation affect polysilicon and module suppliers.
rg3.r.esg.kosong: No ESG or forced labour data can be shown yet.
rg3.r.esg.lain: And {n} more notes in supplier profiles.
rg3.r.n.esg: Quotes come from open sources and are not determinations; read the source before drawing conclusions.
rg3.r.s.radar: New plants, expansions, closures, bankruptcies, acquisitions, and tariff changes. Coverage rests on open web search, not a census.
rg3.r.s.ganggu: Disruptions affecting global ship capacity and rates.
rg3.r.kosong_data: Supply chain risk data is not available yet.

rg3.w.n_penyedia_cat: A provider's involvement in an Indonesian project is marked only where a source exists.
rg3.w.pendamping: Export credit or aid agencies that usually accompany exports (not project facts):
rg3.w.j.hulu: From waste sorting to RDF buyers
rg3.w.s.hulu: Three upstream segments that feed PSEL plants under Presidential Regulation 109/2025.

rg3.met.l1: Landed cost is computed per product unit: freight = 40-foot container rate divided by load per container; insurance = assumed percentage times (FOB + freight); CIF = FOB + freight + insurance.
rg3.met.l2: Import duty uses the trade agreement preferential rate when the origin country is a member and the row has been checked; otherwise the MFN rate per six-digit HS code. An HS code without a readable rate makes the user enter it.
rg3.met.l3: VAT and import income tax art. 22 are computed on the import value (CIF + import duty); both are generally creditable, so the result is shown with and without those taxes.
rg3.met.l4: Country concentration uses the HHI over import partner shares (UN Comtrade) and over listed suppliers per home country; thresholds 1,500 and 2,500.
rg3.met.r1: Total = FOB + freight + insurance + import duty + VAT + income tax art. 22 + inland logistics; duty = bm% x CIF; VAT = vat% x (CIF + duty); income tax = rate% x (CIF + duty). Rupiah = USD x exchange rate.
rg3.met.r2: HHI = sum of (percentage share)^2 over all partners, between 0 and 10,000. Price gap = (Indonesian price - reference world price) / reference world price.
rg3.met.b1: Freight uses a global composite index, not an Asia-to-Indonesia route rate; load per container and insurance are hypotheses that can be changed.
rg3.met.b2: Inland and inter-island logistics have no sourced data yet; the entry port per province is a rough regional split.
rg3.met.b3: Supplier counts per country are not market share or capacity; preferential rates from an aggregator have not been checked against official documents.
rg3.met.s1: Price benchmarks (InfoLink, IRENA, BNEF), Drewry WCI, tariff schedule PMK 26/2022, PMK 131/2024, UN Comtrade; files in public/data/global.

psl.t.hba: Average HBA {hl} per tonne in {tahun}, down from the USD {puncak} peak in {tp}
psl.s.hba: Annual average coal reference price 2014 to 2024 (Directorate General of Minerals and Coal) and the USD 70 per tonne power-sector DMO price since 2018.
psl.n.hba: HBA is the reference price for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR coal, not what power plants pay. The HBA formula changed several times; monthly HBA for 2016 to 2024 was not found in one place. Periods in 2025 and 2026 are only those caught by press releases or news.
psl.t.dmo: DMO price {hl} per tonne, unchanged since {th}; {mt} million tonnes of coal to power plants in {tahun}
psl.s.dmo: Legal basis and changes of the DMO price for power supply, plus domestic coal volumes to power plants.
psl.n.dmo: The 2022 to 2026 decree texts were not found on JDIH; the number and the 30% share for 2026 come from news. What is shown is domestic coal sales to power plants (ESDM Handbook), not the DMO target or yearly realisation. The 2025 figure only runs to October (all sectors) and is not charted.
psl.t.tarif: R-1 1,300 VA tariff {hl} per kWh since {th}; {n} non-subsidised tariff groups since 2017
psl.s.tarif: Tariff at the start of each quarter, 2017 to Q3 2026, for non-subsidised groups (rupiah per kWh), and the gap to the 2024 economic tariff per group.
psl.n.tarif: The quarterly series carries recorded tariff events forward (EST): the value on the first day of each quarter. Q4 2026 is not yet verified. The statistics book gives B-3 and I-3 as Rp1,122.10 while ESDM press releases say Rp1,114.74; the chart uses the press releases. Subsidised tariffs have not changed since 2014 per the statistics book. The economic tariff is the supply cost plus margin.
psl.ey.subsidi: Electricity subsidy in the state budget
psl.t.subsidi: Electricity subsidy {hl} in {tb}, up from {a} in {ta}
psl.s.subsidi: Electricity subsidy value 2020 to 2024 (Directorate General of Electricity), budget versus realisation, combined subsidy and compensation, and subsidised customers.
psl.j.pagu: Budget, subsidy plus compensation, and subsidised customers
psl.n.subsidi: Subsidy per kWh is a simple derivation (EST): subsidy divided by subsidised energy. Compensation is paid separately from the subsidy and no yearly Ministry of Finance figure is in this data; the combined 2023 to 2025 figures are quoted by ESDM officials through the media. Subsidised customers for 2026 and 2027 are proposals, not outturns.
psl.ey.bbm: Coal plant fuel cost versus renewables
psl.t.bbm: At HBA, power plant fuel was {hl} costlier than at the DMO price in {tahun} (DMO {dmo}, HBA {hba} cents/kWh); the largest gap since 2018 equals {pk} billion in {tp}
psl.s.bbm: Coal fuel cost per kWh at the HBA and at the USD 70 DMO price (the gap is the implied DMO subsidy), versus full renewable LCOE.
psl.n.bbm: Formula: price per tonne divided by (7,352 thermal kWh per tonne of 6,322 kcal/kg coal times efficiency), with a hypothetical efficiency of {eta}% (range {lo}% to {hi}%; not measured). Implied subsidy = (HBA minus 70) times coal volume to power plants. Renewable LCOE is the IRENA 2024 world average, and Indonesian geothermal 2024, from the build-cost data.
psl.cv.1: HBA refers to high-calorie coal; power plant coal is usually lower in calories and cheaper, so the gap and the implied subsidy are upper bounds, not measured miner losses.
psl.cv.2: This is fuel only, while renewable LCOE includes capital, operations and fuel: not fully comparable. Coal plant fuel alone shows how far DMO coal sits below renewable cost.
psl.cv.3: HBA is nominal current-year USD, LCOE is constant USD 2024 or 2025. In 2020 HBA was below USD 70, so the gap is shown as 0, not negative.
psl.ey.celah: Data still missing in this section
psl.t.celah: {hl} electricity market data gaps, stated as they are
psl.s.celah: Not filled in and not invented. Each gap says what was tried.
psl.celah.1: Monthly HBA for 2016 to 2024 is not included: the minerba.esdm.go.id portal is under maintenance and the monthly decrees were not found collected. What exists: annual averages 2014 to 2024, monthly 2015, and a few periods in 2025 to 2026.
psl.celah.2: The 2025 to 2026 HBA series covers only periods caught by news or press releases; the 2026 high-calorie class follows the news headlines.
psl.celah.3: The text of the 2022 to 2026 DMO decrees was not found on JDIH; the number 267.K/MB.01/MEM.B/2022 and the 30% share for 2026 come from news, some of which returned 403.
psl.celah.4: DMO volume is domestic sales to power plants and coal burned by PLN (ESDM Handbook); the yearly DMO target and realisation against the quota were not read.
psl.celah.5: No official per-quarter, per-group tariff table for 2017 to 2019 was read; the series is carried forward from events (EST). Full tariffs for the 24 subsidised groups per the ESDM regulation are not yet transcribed.
psl.celah.6: B-3, I-3 and P-2 tariffs: statistics book Rp1,122.10, ESDM press releases Rp1,114.74. Both are recorded; the difference is unexplained.
psl.celah.7: Electricity compensation separate from the subsidy per year was not read from the Ministry of Finance or the central government financial report; only the combined ESDM figures for 2023 to 2025 via media. The 2025 pure subsidy outturn is not available.
psl.celah.8: Subsidised customers: only 2024 (over 42 million) and the 2026 and 2027 proposals; no yearly realised series was found.
psl.celah.9: SAIDI and SAIFI by PLN region or unit are not published openly (the 2024 electricity statistics and RUPTL give only the national figure); not filled in per system. The national figure is on the Reliability page.
psl.celah.10: The 50% tariff discount in June to July 2025 and other stimulus are not modelled.
psl.taut.keandalan: See national SAIDI and SAIFI on the Reliability page

bev.met.l1: Eight stages are read from upstream to downstream: mining, processing, precursor and cathode, cells and packs, vehicles, charging, grid BESS, recycling. Smelter, HPAL, and cell rows come from hilirisasi.json without copying; other rows are curated with a source and retrieval date per row.
bev.met.l2: Trade uses UN Comtrade (Indonesia as reporter, 6-digit HS): HS 2604, 7501, 7502, 7202 from hilirisasi.json, HS 8507.60 from dagang_komponen.json, and HS 2602, 8105.20, 2825.20, 2836.91, 2833.24, 8703.80 harvested fresh with at least a two-second pause.
bev.met.l3: Prices: annual nickel and lithium from bahan_baku.json (Pink Sheet and USGS); BNEF 2025 pack prices; 2026 LME nickel and lithium carbonate points from media, marked as media.
bev.met.l4: Evidence levels: official, study, media, estimate, hypothesis. Media figures use sources that can be opened; unreadable items are listed as gaps.
bev.met.r1: Battery demand (GWh) = 2025 units x growth^(year-2025) x kWh per vehicle / 1,000,000; motorcycles 2 kWh and hybrid/PHEV 1.5 kWh fixed; BESS = scenario target spread evenly over 2026 to 2028.
bev.met.r2: Electric cars per SPKLU = electric-car population of about 223,000 divided by the latest SPKLU points (EST).
bev.met.s1: Curation in scripts/panen/baterai_ev_kurasi.mjs (source per row), UN Comtrade, USGS, Geological Agency via media, BNEF, Gaikindo, Ministry of Transport SRUT, MEMR; file public/data/baterai_ev.json.

bev.met.b2: The cell-versus-demand balance is a hypothesis: kWh per vehicle is an assumption, cell output is not necessarily absorbed domestically, and chemistry must match the vehicle.
bev.met.b3: Installed BESS capacity, recycling capacity, and HS 8711.60 (e-motorcycles; Comtrade returned 403) are unavailable.
lel.title: Renewable energy tender and procurement tracker | METI Directory
lel.deskripsi: Tracker of renewable IPP procurement rounds run by PLN and its subsidiaries: scheme, stage, bidders and winners, prices against the Presidential Regulation 112/2022 ceiling, timeline, prequalified provider lists (DPT), and world auction benchmarks, with sources and evidence levels.
lel.judul: Renewable energy tender and procurement tracker

lel.s.skema: Each bar is split by the latest stage of the round.
lel.s.tabel: Click a round name for its stage history, bidders, price, and project links.
lel.n.tabel: Sources: open news and studies read on 8 Nov 2026 and ESDM geothermal auction data; PLN procurement portals and LPSE were not read. A blank winner means the result was not found, not that none exists.
lel.kosong_harga: No round has a public price yet.

lel.n.liga: Only names stated in open sources; many winners are not announced. A winner of an umbrella programme and of its packages is counted in each round.

lel.n.peserta: A count, not a name list: PLN generally does not publish losing bidders.

lel.t.banding_kosong: No public price to compare yet
lel.s.banding: {n} of {m} rounds have a PPA or bid price stated by a source.
lel.n.banding: Ceiling = year 1-10 coefficient (peluang.json) x location factor F for its capacity tier. Regulation 112/2022 came after the Cirata PPA was signed, so this is a benchmark, not the cap in force then. MWac/MWp basis and FX are not adjusted.
lel.s.patokan: US cents/kWh with F = 1 (Java, Madura, Bali); other regions are multiplied by F up to 1.5. Year 11 onwards is lower.
lel.n.patokan: Source: Regulation 112/2022 annex, transcribed in peluang.json.
lel.s.celah: Stated openly so the numbers shown are not read as stronger than their evidence.
lel.s.linimasa: Rule changes, round stages, and scheduled targets by year.
lel.s.rinci_tahun: Pick a year; events labelled Target are quoted schedules that may not have happened.
lel.s.dunia_harga: Auctions in {n} countries. Only prices whose source gives a US$/MWh value are drawn; other currencies are in the table without FX conversion.
lel.n.dunia_harga: Indonesian tariffs (PPA, including floating solar) and world auction prices (bid LCOE) are not strictly equivalent; read as orders of magnitude only.
lel.s.dunia_kap: Megawatts awarded in the reported auction results.
lel.s.dunia_tabel: From the global supply-chain benchmark file; each row carries its source link and evidence level.
lel.n.dunia_tabel: Prices in the source's own currency; not converted except the US$/MWh the source gives.

iv.deskripsi: Renewable projects closest to being financed: Hypothesis readiness score, automatic financial model, matching financiers, main risks, and permitting status. Not investment advice.
iv.judul: Investment room: renewable projects closest to financing
iv.lead: Planned and permitted projects with a readiness score, automatic financial model, matching financiers, main risks, and permitting status. Every score shows its components.
iv.penafian: The scores and models on this page are open Hypotheses built from public data to explore projects. They are not investment advice, an offer of securities, or a guarantee of results. Do your own due diligence and consult a licensed adviser before deciding.

iv.p.tanpa_model: Matching uses the funding need from the model; no model is available for this project.

iv.r.tanpa: The land risk score is not yet computed for this project because its location data layer is missing.
iv.r.lokasi: The project location is only at {presisi} level, so risk and grid distance may be off.
iv.z.tanpa: No permit record specific to this project in the data; only the stage from the source and the provincial index.
iv.b.lead: Green highlights mark the best value in that row.
iv.b.catatan: Hypothesis scores and models from public data.
iv.met.j: A Hypothesis readiness score with six open components
iv.cara1: Filter planned and permitted projects of 5 MW and above from the integrated projects layer, in technologies that have a sourced cost basis and benchmark price.
iv.cara2: Run the default /model-keuangan model per project: IPP, Perpres 112/2022 benchmark price by MW and location factor, cost from build-cost data.
iv.cara3: Turn each input into a 0 to 1 component, then take the weighted average. Components without data are left out and weights recomputed.
iv.cara4: Match each project with institutions, schemes, and export credit agencies by technology, typical ticket size (0.1 to 10 times the funding need), and owner country.
iv.cara.f1: Score = sum(weight x value) / sum of weights of available components; no score if fewer than 4 components. High is 60 and above, medium 40 to 60.
iv.met.cara.izin: Average of the stage value (permitted 1, planned 0.4) and the provincial permitting index divided by 100.
iv.met.cara.harga: (Year-1 benchmark price / LCOE - 0.6) / 0.8, clamped to 0 to 1.
iv.met.cara.lahan: 1 minus the project risk score divided by 100 (forest, peat, customary land, natural hazards).
iv.met.cara.sumber: The provincial resource norm from the Radar (PVOUT and gap for solar, gap for other technologies).
iv.met.cara.pendanaan: Recorded external financing or JETP 1; listed developer 0.6; owner name 0.4; RUPTL 0.3; otherwise 0.
iv.met.cara.jaringan: 1 minus the distance to the nearest 150 kV substation divided by 100 km; only for regency-level or point locations.
iv.cara.b1: Storage, nuclear, and waste-to-energy are excluded: there is no sourced cost basis or benchmark price for the automatic model.
iv.cara.b2: Bioenergy is listed without a financial model because its operating cost is not available; other empty cost cells are filled with the midpoint of the sourced range and flagged.
iv.cara.b3: Projects without a verified province are excluded; province-level locations are not used for grid distance, and OSM substations are only harvested for some islands.
iv.cara.b4: The model puts all capex in year 0, with no debt, no construction period, and 22 percent tax. It is not a bankable feasibility study.
iv.cara.b5: Matching financiers reflect data fit, not an offer or commitment. Weights and thresholds are Hypotheses that can change.

sur.p.j.atap: Rooftop solar: quota per system, actuals and rules

sur.p.j.ruptl: RUPTL rooftop quota 2025 to 2034 (MW per year)
sur.p.n.kuota: Quota and actuals are not on the same basis: the Director General quota is per system cluster, actuals are PLN customers and cumulative. Do not read the gap as remaining quota.
sur.p.n.ruptl: The RUPTL document carries only yearly totals and four regions; the per-cluster detail is in the decision above.
sur.p.ke_aturan: Open Energy Ministry Reg. 2/2024 in the regulation directory
sur.p.j.cni: C&I, captive and corporate offtake: {n} solar contracts recorded
sur.p.s.cni: Corporate contracts and aggregates are read from korporat.json; industry holds 72 percent of PLN rooftop capacity as of May 2025.
sur.p.n.cni: Only contracts readable from open sources; private portfolios are incomplete.
sur.p.j.util: {n} solar projects in the METI base, {g} GW if all are counted
sur.p.s.util: Capacity per status from proyek.json; the table lists projects of 10 MW and above other than floating.
sur.p.j.tp: {n} reservoirs with potential, about {g} GW at 20 percent of area
sur.p.s.tp: Potential assumes 20 percent of reservoir area; the 13.9 GW RUPTL figure is compared, not added.
sur.p.cara_tp: Reservoir area x 20 percent x power density
sur.p.n.tp: METI still asks for legal certainty on dam use for floating solar; potential is not a permit.
sur.g.j: The {g} GW solar programme: village cooperatives, targets, first phase and implementers
sur.g.s: Details from dated coverage and program_analisis.json; no presidential regulation yet, so many numbers are government claims.
sur.po.s.prov: Global Solar Atlas, one capital-city point per province: a relative indication, not a province average.
sur.po.cara: Global Solar Atlas 2.0, long-term data at the provincial capital point (CC BY 4.0)
sur.po.n.prov: A provincial capital is not the best project site: use it to compare, then check the specific location.
sur.po.s.kab: A 0 to 100 score combining PVOUT, supply gap, generation cost, price, access, market, EIA and regional rules; components without data are dropped.
sur.po.n.kab: Most scores use province-level data; a per-regency map is not available. The score helps screening, not choosing a site.
sur.po.ke_terapung: Floating solar potential in the Projects tab
sur.bi.j.capex: Solar build cost by scale (USD/kW, mid value)
sur.bi.s.capex: Indonesian scales compared with foreign benchmarks; each row carries its evidence level and source.
sur.bi.n.capex: Indonesian costs come from the METI calculator and project totals divided by capacity (Hypothesis or EST); foreign benchmarks are not Indonesian prices.
sur.bi.tarif: {n} PLN tariff classes are available in the rooftop solar calculator.
sur.bi.j.lama: From idea to commercial operation by scale
sur.bi.s.lama: Month ranges labelled Hypothesis: METI judgement from project patterns, not yet validated per project.
sur.bi.cara_lama: METI judgement from project patterns; stages run in parallel
sur.bi.n.lama: The total is not the sum of all stages because some run in parallel.
sur.bi.ke_bab43: The solar project path, stage by stage (chapter 43)
sur.bi.s.model: Who pays what and who carries the risk; a summary of the business model chapter of the solar topic.
sur.bi.cara_model: METI editorial summary, not an article quotation
sur.bi.n.model: Model comparison scores are a METI Hypothesis. Summaries are truncated; read the full chapter for conditions and risks.
sur.k.j.dagang: {n} trade policies from {m} jurisdictions touching the solar chain
sur.k.s.dagang: US anti-dumping and countervailing duties on cells and modules from Indonesia, forced labour bans, the EU carbon border mechanism, local content and import duty exemptions.
sur.k.h.dampak: Indonesian solar exports to the United States (HS 854143)
sur.k.j.dampak: Indonesian solar exports, to the US and elsewhere (USD million)
sur.k.n.dampak: Export values are UN Comtrade via dagang_komponen.json; the duties target PT Blue Sky Solar and PT REC Solar. The final order status needs checking in the Federal Register.
sur.k.ke_dagang: All trade policies and agreements in the global chain
sur.k.j.tkdn: Module local content threshold test from {n} active certificates
sur.k.s.tkdn: How many certificates and how much capacity pass if the local content threshold is raised, against annual demand.
sur.k.hip: Hypothesis: equal weight per certificate because per-factory capacity is not open, and demand is one number (17 GW over three years).
sur.k.cara_tkdn: share of certificates passing x capacity against annual demand; formula in inti/simulasi_tkdn_rumus.js
sur.k.ke_sim: Full simulation of the effect on capex and IRR
sur.k.j.reg: Core regulations and the quota decision
sur.k.s.reg: Regulations are referenced from the METI regulation directory; the quota decision is a Director General decision, not a ministerial regulation.
sur.k.ke_topik: Timeline and rules in the solar topic
sur.d.j.pensiun: Solar capacity past its design life (cumulative MW)
sur.d.s.pensiun: From IRENASTAT installed history with 25 and 30 year lives; the big wave comes only after 2050.
sur.d.tambah25: Extra if the life is 25 years
sur.d.pembanding: global benchmark in the recycling file
sur.d.n.pensiun: Tonnage is NOT calculated because the module mass per MW is not sourced; only MW past design life is shown. Early loss is not modelled.
sur.d.s.pelaku: The two players on record work on EV batteries; no solar panel recycler has been read yet.
sur.d.n.pelaku: No dedicated solar panel recycler or rule was found; this list marks the nearest capability, not a panel service.
sur.i.s: Raw material, rooftop solar and 100 GW programme issues; the speaking party is named and claims carry an evidence level.
sur.i.n: High-level issues concern legal certainty or supply; the evidence level shows how strong the source is, not how true the claim is.
sur.dari_program: The solar chain end to end for the 100 GW programme: silica sand to modules, rooftop, village cooperatives and issues
sur.dari_tek: Solar end to end (raw materials, factories, projects, rooftop quota, recycling)
sur.dari_rantai: The solar chain end to end: see the Solar module
sur.td.j: Role in the Indonesian solar chain
sur.met.l1: Eight stages are read from upstream to downstream: silica raw material, polysilicon to modules, projects (rooftop, C&I, utility, floating, the 100 GW programme), potential, cost, policy and local content, recycling and issues.
sur.met.l2: Players, factories, balance, prices, trade policy, potential, cost and recycling are read directly from existing files; this module adds only new data (silica, rooftop quota per cluster, rooftop actuals, programme details) without copying.
sur.met.l3: Every number carries an evidence level and a dated source; numbers that differ across sources are shown side by side, not averaged.
sur.met.l4: Silica sand exports and the 100 GW programme annual targets are left blank on purpose because no sourced number exists; the annual curve in the Projects tab is a Hypothesis.
sur.met.r1: Module balance = COD-year solar demand (RUPTL, plus the 100 GW curve as a Hypothesis) x a factor of 1 MWp module per MWp of plant versus domestic factory capacity; gap = max(0, demand minus capacity).
sur.met.r2: Local content test = share of active certificates with local content above the threshold x capacity against annual demand (equal weight per certificate).
sur.met.s1: Curation in scripts/panen/surya_modul_kurasi.mjs (source per row); DPR (rooftop quota), ESDM and PLN via media, Ministry of Industry via media, IMA, DJEBTKE, Global Solar Atlas; file public/data/surya_modul.json.
sur.met.b1: Decision 279.K/2024 is read from a DPR publication, not from a copy of the decision itself; whether the quotas are cumulative or annual additions is not stated explicitly.
sur.met.b2: Rooftop actuals come from officials' statements on different dates and are not uniform; the 1.3 GW milestone (April 2026) is not reconciled with the 895 MW from the same event.
sur.met.b3: Silica tonnage per province exists only for Riau Islands; UN Comtrade and bisnis.com returned 403 so harvesting stopped per policy.
swe.title: Waste to energy end to end | METI Directory
swe.deskripsi: Waste to energy end to end: waste generation and landfills, PSEL/WtE plants, RDF/SRF, landfill biogas, incinerators, the 33 Danantara cities, winning consortia, Perpres 109/2025, tipping fee and power price, global technology suppliers, and resident opposition, with evidence levels and sources.
swe.judul: Waste to energy end to end
swe.lead: The METI base lists {n} PSEL projects: {op} operating and {k} under construction. The Danantara programme targets {kota} cities under Perpres 109/2025.
swe.kosong: Waste-to-energy module data is not available yet.
swe.hip.cara: METI assumption for the worked example; not project data.
swe.u.proyek: PSEL projects in the base, {ton} tonnes a day in total
swe.u.miliar_td: IDR billion per tonne a day
swe.s.j.angka: {n} open-dumping landfills; only {p} percent of waste is managed properly
swe.s.s.angka: One official Environment Ministry figure (2023) is used, not mixed with press figures.
swe.s.tak_ket: Difference between generation and managed waste (METI calculation).
swe.s.j.grafik: Provinces with the largest PSEL capacity
swe.s.s.grafik: Tonnes a day of PSEL projects in the base, top ten provinces; hover for details.
swe.s.n.grafik: Capacity is project design (including planned), not waste already processed.
swe.s.s.prov: Project count, capacity and status by province, read from psel.json.
swe.s.n.prov: Cities without a capacity figure count as zero in the tonnes-a-day column.
swe.j.j.jenis: Four routes turn waste into energy
swe.j.s.jenis: PSEL, RDF/SRF, landfill biogas and incinerators differ in output, cost and risk.
swe.j.n.jenis: The route split is a METI summary of the linked sources; routes can overlap.
swe.j.s.fas: Capacities that differ between sources are shown side by side, not merged.
swe.j.n.fas: Some items were read only from a headline or search summary; the evidence level is on the badge.
swe.j.s.hulu: Upstream segments from pemasok_wte.json; players not yet sourced are left empty.
swe.k.j.ringkas: {n} PSEL projects in the base from a {kota}-city programme
swe.k.s.ringkas: The full list of 33 cities is not in open sources; what appears is the projects already recorded.
swe.k.s.grafik: The twelve cities with the largest capacity; hover for MW and status.
swe.k.s.daftar: Filter by status; sort by clicking a column heading.
swe.k.n.daftar: Status follows psel.json (press and Wikipedia PSN list); cities without status have no readable source yet.
swe.k.n.peta: Coordinates are at regency or city precision, not site location.
swe.c.n.tahap: Values and counts are press reports, not contract values; different sources give different figures.
swe.c.s.kons: Consortia are linked to projects in psel.json; the country follows the recorded technology supplier.
swe.c.n.kons: The role of consortium members and technology suppliers is not fully confirmed by sources; an empty column means no data.
swe.c.s.peng: Developers recorded in psel.json; click a name for the profile.
swe.a.s.reg: Read from regulasi.json; Perpres 109/2025 replaces the two earlier Perpres.
swe.a.n.reg: The official text is on BPK JDIH; this page summarises and does not replace the articles.
swe.a.s.kunci: Summarised from legal commentary and press; refer to the articles for certainty.
swe.a.s.lama: The old tariff was judged too low; only two of 15 old projects operate.
swe.t.j.harga: Perpres tariffs: from 13.35 to 20 cents per kWh
swe.t.s.harga: Regulatory tariffs, not project PPA prices; per-project PPA prices are not yet available.
swe.t.n.harga: USD cents per kWh. The Perpres 35/2018 formula for capacity above 20 MW is shown as written.
swe.t.j.tip: Tipping fee removed, burden moves to PLN compensation
swe.t.s.tip: Per-tonne tipping fee and per-project PPA price are not in open sources.
swe.t.j.hitung: Electricity revenue and energy per tonne of waste
swe.t.s.hitung: METI calculation labelled EST/Hypothesis from psel.json capacity and the Perpres 109/2025 price.
swe.t.contoh: Annual energy {gwh} GWh = MW x capacity factor {cf}% x 8.76; times a price of {h} cents per kWh. The capacity factor is a Hypothesis.
swe.t.per_ton: {mw} MW over 24 hours divided by {ton} tonnes a day, at a Hypothesis capacity factor.
swe.t.cara_ton: MW x 24 x capacity factor / tonnes a day
swe.t.j.gr: Electricity per tonne of waste by project (EST)
swe.t.n.hitung: Only projects with both MW and tonnes a day in psel.json are calculated; figures are not operating results.
swe.t.j.biaya: Investment per capacity and programme value
swe.t.s.biaya: Investment values from press; cost per tonne a day is a METI calculation (EST).
swe.t.cara_inv: Rupiah investment divided by tonnes a day
swe.t.n.biaya: Not final contract values. PSEL cost components are not yet in biaya_bangun.json.
swe.p.s.negara: Suppliers per country and linked Indonesian projects; export credit agency involvement is not yet sourced.
swe.p.n.negara: The supplier list is METI curation, not every provider worldwide; being listed does not mean they supply an Indonesian project.
swe.p.s.pem: Technology, components and linked Indonesian projects per supplier.
swe.p.n.pem: A supplier's role in a project is written as in the source; some are unconfirmed.
swe.p.j.kait: Whose technology the Danantara programme uses
swe.p.s.kait: Danantara statements and tender reports; the component import flow is unknown.
swe.i.s.tolak: Claims by residents, campaigners and government are written as their own claims, not facts verified by METI.
swe.i.n.tolak: Parties named may send a response through the platform correction form; responses are published alongside.
swe.i.j.isu: {n} PSEL issues from the issues base
swe.i.s.isu: PSEL tariff, land and schedule by region plus the tipping fee issue, read from isu.json.
swe.i.n.isu: Details and timeline of each issue are on the issues page.
swe.met.l1: Generation, managed waste and open-dumping landfills use one official Environment Ministry figure (2023); 2024 press figures differ in coverage and are not mixed.
swe.met.l2: PSEL projects are read from psel.json, consortia linked by id, suppliers from global/pemasok_wte.json, and regulations and issues from their own files.
swe.met.l3: New items (RDF, landfill gas, resident opposition, Danantara programme) have source URLs and evidence levels; what was not found is written as a gap.
swe.met.l4: Annual energy = MW x capacity factor x 8.76; electricity per tonne = MW x 24 x capacity factor / tonnes a day; the 85% capacity factor is a Hypothesis.
swe.met.r1: Revenue = GWh x 1,000 x cents per kWh / 100; the 20-cent price is from Perpres 109/2025.
swe.met.r2: Investment per tonne a day = rupiah investment / tonnes a day, labelled EST.
swe.met.s1: Environment Ministry, BPK JDIH, ESDM, Danantara via press, Mongabay, Katadata, Bisnis.com, legal commentary and journals; each item carries a source and evidence level.
swe.met.b1: The full list of 33 cities is not available; the base holds 23 projects.
swe.met.b2: Some items were read only from a headline or search summary because sites block automated fetching.
swe.met.b3: Tariffs are Perpres provisions, not project PPA prices; per-tonne tipping fee is not available.
swe.td.j: Plays a role in the waste-to-energy chain
swe.tk.tl: Waste to energy end to end (cities, consortia, price, suppliers, issues)
swe.isu.d: See context in the waste-to-energy module
hdr.title: End-to-end hydropower | METI Directory
hdr.deskripsi: End-to-end hydropower: potential and river basins, PLTA and PLTM plants, Upper Cisokan pumped storage, PUPR dams, RUPTL and policy, cost and LCOE, turbine suppliers, financing, and social-environmental issues, with evidence levels and sources.
hdr.lead: Indonesia hydropower potential is about {p} GW, with {t} GW installed ({pc}% of potential); uptake is held back by land, permits, financing, and social-environmental issues. Nine tabs trace river basins, plants, pumped storage, dams, cost, suppliers, and issues, each figure carrying its evidence level and source.
hdr.kosong: Hydropower data could not be loaded. Reload the page later.
hdr.s.s.angka: All versions of each figure are shown with their sources, plus government targets.
hdr.s.s.prov: Potential from two hydro topic sources; projects counted from the integrated project base.
hdr.s.n.prov: The two potential columns come from different sources and are not added.
hdr.s.s.das: HydroBASINS level 07 sub-basins hosting hydro plants, with water vulnerability scores.
hdr.s.n.das: This table lists basins that already host plants, not undeveloped basin potential. The water vulnerability score is a METI computation (EST).
hdr.s.air_energi: Open the Water and energy page
hdr.s.n.peta: Location precision is shown on each point; province or regency precision is not the dam site.
hdr.p.s.ringkas: Capacity by status from the integrated project base (RUPTL, GEM, proyek.json).
hdr.p.s.daftar: Size class uses a {batas} MW threshold (METI grouping). Filter by status and class.
hdr.p.n.daftar: The project base can list one plant twice from different sources; status and COD follow each row source, none chosen silently.
hdr.m.s.kandidat: Upper Cisokan, Matenggeng, Grindulu, and scattered West Java pumped storage per the RUPTL 2025-2034.
hdr.m.s.cisokan: Design, contractors, schedule, and financing, each item with its source.
hdr.m.n.cisokan: The schedule differs across sources; no version is chosen silently.
hdr.m.j.dana: World Bank and AIIB projects for pumped storage
hdr.m.s.dana: Read from the METI funding base; the World Bank status of Matenggeng is recorded as cancelled.
hdr.m.n.dana: Values are commitments per the source, not disbursements.
hdr.b.j.angka: Hydro at PUPR dams: aggregate figures
hdr.b.s.angka: PUPR preliminary studies and the RUPTL; figures differ by year and dam coverage.
hdr.b.n.angka: Figures are preliminary studies not yet coordinated with PLN; floating PV is far larger than hydro at dams.
hdr.b.s.prioritas: Dams tendered by the Ministry of Public Works under the PPP scheme (March 2025).
hdr.b.n.prioritas: Per-dam capacity is available only for Leuwikeris; the rest has not been announced.
hdr.b.j.contoh: Example dam with an operating plant
hdr.b.s.contoh: Jatigede, a PUPR dam with a 2 x 55 MW plant operated by PLN.
hdr.r.j.ruptl: {n} hydro projects in the RUPTL, {mw} MW
hdr.r.s.ruptl: RE Base scenario: capacity by COD year and project list.
hdr.r.s.reg: Power purchase, water-resource infrastructure partnerships, and community micro-hydro.
hdr.r.n.reg: Several hydro power purchase regulations are revoked; the Water Resources Law is not yet in the regulation base.
hdr.c.j.hitung: Hydro LCOE: METI calculation on IRENA data
hdr.c.s.hitung: Capex, capacity factor, and opex from IRENA; WACC and life are assumptions.
hdr.c.k.rentang_ket: From low capex with high capacity factor to high capex with low capacity factor.
hdr.c.k.rp_ket: Rate Rp {kurs} per US$ (hypothesis in biaya_bangun).
hdr.c.n.rumus: LCOE = (capex x CRF + annual opex) / annual energy; CRF = r(1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1). This is an EST computation, not a selling price.
hdr.c.j.skenario: PLTA and PLTM across three cases
hdr.c.s.skenario: Capex from IRENA 2024; PLTM uses the PLTA capacity factor because IRENA gives no separate figure.
hdr.c.n.skenario: Not Indonesian data: capex and capacity factor are world or other-Asia averages.
hdr.c.j.sens: Capital cost and WACC drive LCOE
hdr.c.s.sens: Mid-case LCOE by WACC, and the civil, mechanical, and electrical cost split.
hdr.c.n.sens: The cost split is from a 2021 European sample (IHA via IRENA), not Indonesia.
hdr.t.s.pem: Read from the global supplier base; home country shown with flag.
hdr.t.n.pem: Being listed as a hydro supplier does not mean supplying a specific Indonesian project.
hdr.t.s.kon: Civil and EPC contractors found in sources.
hdr.t.n.kon: Electromechanical packages (turbines and generators) have not been found for these projects.
hdr.n.j.lembaga: World Bank, JICA, ADB, and Chinese banks
hdr.n.s.daftar: Read from the METI funding base by id.
hdr.n.n.daftar: Cancelled projects are excluded from the chart; values are commitments, not disbursements, and not every row is hydro only.
hdr.i.s.baru: New items sourced from news and reports, with party claims kept labelled.
hdr.i.n.baru: Named parties can send a correction or response through the platform correction form; responses are published alongside.
hdr.i.s.kasus: Summary of causes and impacts from the case chapter of the hydro topic.
hdr.i.n.kasus: Details, timelines, and sources are in the hydro topic.
hdr.i.j: {n} issues in the METI issue base
hdr.i.s: Read from isu.json by id; details on the issue page.
hdr.i.n: Party claims stay labelled on the issue page.
hdr.met.l1: Potential and installed capacity use every version found (Ministry of ESDM, Undip, IRENA); none is chosen silently.
hdr.met.l2: Projects and capacity are read from the integrated project base (RUPTL, GEM, proyek.json); large class at 10 MW or more; basins from air_energi.json; pumped storage from the RUPTL research file.
hdr.met.l3: PUPR dams use aggregate preliminary-study figures; no per-dam list is available except the 10 PPP priority dams.
hdr.met.l4: LCOE = (capex x CRF + opex) / annual energy, with capex and capacity factor from IRENA and WACC a METI assumption (Hypothesis).
hdr.met.r1: CRF = r(1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1) with a 40-year economic life.
hdr.met.r2: Annual energy per kW = 8.76 x capacity factor (percent) x 10 kWh.
hdr.met.s1: Ministry of ESDM, PUPR, IRENA, PLN RUPTL, Global Energy Monitor, World Bank, AIIB, ADB, JICA, JDIH BPK, company releases, and media; each item carries its source and evidence level.
hdr.met.b1: Undeveloped potential per river basin was not found; the basin table lists basins already hosting plants.
hdr.met.b2: Turbine supplier per Indonesian project unit and the Upper Cisokan electromechanical package have not been found.
hdr.met.b3: The Upper Cisokan COD differs across sources; Kayan and Mentarang status comes from news and advocacy reports.
tk.tl.hidro: End-to-end hydropower (potential, plants, pumped storage, dams, LCOE, issues)
isu.d.hdr: See more hydro issues in the end-to-end hydropower module
ang.title: Wind end to end | METI Directory
ang.deskripsi: Wind (onshore and offshore) end to end: potential and Global Wind Atlas by province, the Sidrap, Tolo and Tanah Laut projects and the RUPTL pipeline, turbine, tower and blade supply chain, cost and LCOE, auctions and local content, ports and logistics, policy, issues and players, with evidence levels and sources.
ang.lead: Onshore wind potential is about {p} GW and offshore about {l} GW, yet only {t} MW is installed and RUPTL 2025-2034 targets {r} GW. Nine tabs cover potential, projects, supply chain, cost, auctions, logistics, policy, issues and players, every figure with a source and evidence level.
ang.lead_kosong: Wind data is not available yet.
ang.kosong: Wind data is not available yet.
ang.u.proyek_l: Wind projects in the base ({mw} MW operating)
ang.p.j.angka: Onshore potential {d} GW and offshore {l} GW, almost none built
ang.p.s.angka: Every version of the potential figure is shown with its source; installed capacity comes from IRENASTAT.
ang.p.j.target: Delivery of 0.15 GW against targets of up to 28 GW
ang.p.s.target: Installed capacity, named RUPTL projects and targets from RUEN, RUPTL and press reports.
ang.p.n.target: The 7.2 GW RUPTL figure is the aggregate in the official FAQ; the per-province tables name only a small part. The 5 GW by 2030 target comes from press and has not been read in full text.
ang.p.g.label: Wind capacity (GW)
ang.p.j.prov: Wind speed at 100 m and potential across 38 provinces

ang.p.j.kab: {n} regencies and cities in the Global Wind Atlas

ang.p.cara_atlas: Global Wind Atlas v4, mean speed at 100 m, 5x5 pixel window
ang.pr.s.unggul: Two operating utility wind farms in South Sulawesi and one tendered project in South Kalimantan.
ang.pr.n.unggul: Profiles are read from the wind topic; turbines and suppliers come from the releases and press cited in the footer.
ang.pr.turbin_belum: Not yet fixed (more than 6 MW per unit planned)

ang.pr.j.daftar: All wind projects in the base
ang.pr.s.daftar: Filter by status; sort by capacity or COD.
ang.pr.n.daftar: The owner may be a developer status per RUPTL rather than a company name. The base lists some projects more than once.
ang.pr.j.ruptl: RUPTL names {n} MW of wind, its aggregate is {r} GW
ang.pr.s.ruptl: Named wind projects in the per-province detail tables, COD from the RE Base scenario.
ang.pr.n.ruptl: The gap between named projects and the 7.2 GW aggregate shows most additions have no site in the document yet.
ang.pr.s.peta: Pins by status; hover or focus for details.
ang.pr.n.peta: Coordinates are regency-level or GEM points, not site boundaries.
ang.r.j.komp: Six components and who makes them
ang.r.s.komp: Global suppliers from the supplier base; only towers are made in Indonesia.
ang.r.n.komp: Supplier counts follow the METI base (wind segment), not market share.
ang.r.cara_belum: METI reading of the available sources
ang.r.j.pem: {n} wind suppliers in the METI base
ang.r.s.pem: By country of origin and component; the units column is filled only when a release names them.
ang.r.neg.label: Suppliers per country
ang.r.n.pem: Installed units in Indonesia are verified only for Siemens Gamesa (Sidrap and Tolo).
ang.r.s.imp: UN Comtrade, Indonesia as reporter; annual value in US$ million.
ang.r.imp.label: HS 850231 imports (US$ million)

ang.r.cara_imp: Timing alignment with Sidrap and Tolo construction; not proof of cause
ang.b.j.lcoe: Wind electricity cost: estimates versus real tariffs
ang.b.s.lcoe: Four calculated scenarios (Estimate and Hypothesis) beside case tariffs and the Perpres 112/2022 reference price.
ang.b.g.label: US cents per kWh
ang.b.cara: WACC, opex and lifetime assumptions are METI hypotheses

nkl.lead: Indonesia has no commercial nuclear plant yet. The 2025-2034 RUPTL holds {mw} MW, the National Energy Council cites a {gw} GW goal for 2060, and {n} BRIN research reactors operate. Ten tabs trace plans, licensing, sites, fuel, opinion, comparisons, cost and safety, each figure with source and evidence level.

nkl.l.s.kerja: Workshops and missions on record; no dedicated regulation was found.
